docs.title: Project overview
docs.text:
Jellyfin Enhanced (JE) adds browsing and playback tools, personal settings and service integrations to Jellyfin. You install it on the server to add features to that server's web interface. Selected server features also work with native clients; see compatibility.

JE is an independent community project by n00bcodr and contributors, not an official Jellyfin or Seerr product. The project manifest describes its origins as a combination of the Jellyfin Enhanced and Jellyfin Elsewhere userscripts.

Start with the documentation index, quick start or feature guide. JE is licensed under GPL-3.0.

docs.text:
Project How it connects to JE Seerr Requests, discovery, recommendations, automatic requests and watchlist sync. Configure the service and link each requesting user's Seerr account. Sonarr, Radarr, Bazarr and Shoko Library-management links, tags, downloads and release-calendar data. See the *arr guide. Plugin Pages Optional delivery for Bookmarks, Calendar, Requests, Hidden Content, Recommendations, Activity and Catch Up. Custom Tabs Optional delivery of those pages through custom Home tabs. JE also has native Home tabs that need neither companion. File Transformation Required by optional companions such as Plugin Pages and Custom Tabs. JE itself does not require it. KefinTweaks Displays your watchlist. JE's watchlist sync works without it.

Catch Up and Activity are built into JE. In Catch Up, you can mark unwatched titles watched, dismiss them in this browser, add them to your watchlist or open details.

How it works

JE adds its client scripts as the server serves the web interface. It does not require File Transformation for this.

Watchlist sync reads and writes Jellyfin's Likes flag without requiring KefinTweaks. Catch Up's optional server activity log is separate from outbound analytics; see the collection and privacy explanation.

See JE pages & tabs for page masters, delivery choices and requirements. For themes and other projects by n00bcodr, use Related projects.

docs.title: Admin Media Tags tab
docs.text:
The Media Tags tab of the Jellyfin Enhanced configuration page (#/configurationpage?name=Jellyfin%20Enhanced&jeSection=media-tags) holds every server-wide poster tag setting. It is built from small section modules, so a new setting is a one-line declaration. This page is for contributors; administrators should read Tags & badges.

The Overview section, with the live preview of a new user's cards.

The Groups section: each row opens that group's server settings.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
• Where it lives. Configuration/configPage.html has a media-tags tab button and, after its <form>, the tab's content <div id="media-tags" class="jellyfin-tab-content je-mt-tab"> holding .je-tag-admin. - The page's whole-form Save, its unsaved-changes badge (a snapshot of the form's controls), search highlighting and implicit Enter-submit never see the tab's controls. - jeAdmin.js lists the tab in the sidebar's Appearance group, after Display. The page adds a tree of the tab's seven sections under that entry ([data-je-mt-tree]), and marks the shown one from the je-media-tags-section event.
  • The page's look, not its own. The tab draws no title row or section tabs of its own on a desktop: the sidebar's tree is its navigation, as for the page's other tabs. Its cards, setting rows, switches, fields, buttons, scope badges and focus rings use the configuration page's values (admin-tags.css). - Every section opens with its first card (lead: 'card' in TABS): the section's <h2> stays for screen readers and names its panel, keyboard focus from a sidebar link lands on that card's title, and the save status (All changes saved / Saving…) sits on that card's header row. Groups' rows sit inside one Tag groups card; Overview's intro is the page's tab-intro banner, which the page's Descriptions switch hides along with the tab's help text. - Below a 901 px window (where the page's sidebar becomes its menu) the sections are the page's chip row at the top of the tab, with the save status (Saved) at its end; the tablist itself holds only the section buttons.
  • Drawn on first open. When the tab first opens, configPage.html (jeMountMediaTags) waits for the JE client bundle (already running on dashboard pages: JE.t, core/tag-layout.js, the panel's preview). It then loads js/enhanced/admintags/admin-tags.css and admin-tags.js, and calls JE.adminTags.mountTab(tab). - admin-tags.js loads the files in SECTION_FILES once per document. - Opening the tab again, or showing the page again with the tab open (pageshow), calls mountTab again, which reloads the settings. - Only the shown page element is live. Jellyfin keeps earlier views in the document, so a newer view of the configuration page tears down the previous tab (after saving) and builds its own, keeping control ids unique.
  • Saving one field at a time. Every control writes one PluginConfiguration field into the tab's working copy and saves it after a 400 ms pause through POST /JellyfinEnhanced/admin/configuration. - The server writes only the changed fields on top of the configuration it holds at that moment, inside the same critical section as every configuration save. So another administrator's changes to other fields are kept, as are the server's own writes (a maintenance window ending clears its toggle, the translation refresh task sets its signal, analytics records its state), which take the same lock. - Each field carries the value the tab read before it was edited. If someone else changed that field meanwhile, the server refuses it and the tab shows Changed elsewhere with Keep mine and Take theirs. For one field it names the field and both values, as Keep and Use . - A change that is not saved (refused, or changed elsewhere) floats as a bar where the page's Save dock floats, centred on the settings column, with both values for every field and its buttons; a field being edited is scrolled clear of it. The tab's sidebar entry shows a dot (a screen-reader note says "not saved") so it is seen from any other tab. - Unsaved edits live in a store shared by every view, so a failed save survives moving between sections and links. The store belongs to the signed-in administrator on this server: - An identity change (JE.session.onUserChange, and a check of the ApiClient user and server before every save and view) empties it and the live view. Requests started before it are ignored when they answer. - Every answer (a save, the settings for a first view or a returning one, the preview's Tag Styles) is checked against the session it was asked in, with the ApiClient identity read again first. A server switch that JE.session has not reported yet is caught there too. When someone is signed in by then, the tab loads again for them.
  • Living beside the whole-form Save. The configuration page still saves its own form as a whole: it reads the saved configuration, overlays its own fields and writes the whole document. - Its whole-document writes run inside JE.adminTags.holdSaves(fn): Save, Apply the above, Apply all plugin settings and the Overview's cache quick action. - Media Tags edits not saved yet are saved first, so the fresh read already has them. Field saves started meanwhile wait until the write is done, then go out with their Expected values intact, because the write put back what the server had. - A whole-configuration write therefore never puts an older Media Tags value back, and apply-user-settings still refuses Media Tags fields (MediaTagsPageFields.Allowed). - After a save, the tab dispatches je-media-tags-store ({type, values, state}), and the Display tab's Media Tags card summary follows the saved values. - The Save dock and the "refresh" hint are hidden on the tab unless another tab has unsaved changes.
  • The preview column is internal.createTagPreview from settingspanel/ui-panel-tag-preview.js with a source option. It draws a new user's document seeded from the configuration (JE.adminTags.seedUser, mirroring LoadUserSettingsDocument) and restores the signed-in user's settings afterwards. - Each draw loads missing base styles for the groups enabled by that draft, including edits awaiting a save, independently of the administrator's personal group switches. This only loads CSS: it does not activate disabled renderers or fetch their data. - The hub preview and item editor keep following the user's own enabled groups. - From a tab width of 840 px (a 1400 px window beside Jellyfin's drawer and the settings sidebar) the preview sits beside the settings. Below that it collapses under a sticky toggle. The sticky preview sits under the configuration page's sticky header (on a phone, under its menu bar) and is capped to fit there, so at the end of a short section it does not ride up under the header; its explanations sit in How looks are chosen.
  • Addresses. - &jeSection=media-tags&tab=<id> opens one of the tab's sections, and &group=<id> a Groups panel (or a section marked data-je-anchor). &tab=<id> without jeSection opens any other tab of the page. - A section asked for by the address is opened once per address, so returning to the tab keeps the section chosen since (sessionStorage JE_mediaTagsAdminTab). - Links to the configuration page itself open in place, because navigating would rebuild the view and drop unsaved changes on other tabs: the Display card, What's New entries, the tab's own links to main-page settings (&jeSection=TMDB_API_KEY), the Enhanced panel's pointers to the tab (the panel sits over the page), and the older &jeSection= ids of the old main form's Media Tags controls. The handler acts only for the view shown and leaves links inside another view alone. - The old address #/configurationpage?name=JellyfinEnhancedMediaTags[&tab=<section>][&group=<id>] is still registered (PluginPageInfo, outside the menu). It serves Configuration/mediaTagsPage.html, which only forwards to &jeSection=media-tags with the same tab and group (replacing itself in the history).

docs.title: Add a section
docs.text:
1. Create js/enhanced/admintags/sections/<name>.js (no hyphens in directory names; file names may have them) as a self-contained IIFE:

    (function(JE) {
    'use strict';
    const A = JE.adminTags;
    if (!A) return;
    A.registerSection({
        id: 'group-awards',
        tab: 'groups',            // overview, layout, groups, rules, colours, badges, server
        order: 55,                // position within the tab
        title: 'Awards',
        hint: 'Awards ribbons from Wikidata and MDBList.',
        group: { id: 'awards', summary: (ctx) => '…', sample: () => [['status', 'Oscar']] }, // Groups tab rows only
        fields: [
            { id: 'awardsTagsEnabled', key: 'AwardsTagsEnabled', type: 'enable', label: 'Awards ribbons for new users' },
            { id: 'awardsTagsRefreshHours', key: 'AwardsTagsRefreshHours', type: 'number', min: 1, max: 168, fallback: 24, label: 'Refresh every' },
        ],
        render(ctx, body) { /* optional custom controls into body */ },
        refresh(ctx, body) { /* optional: redraw after any change */ },
    });
})(window.JellyfinEnhanced);

  2. Add the file to SECTION_FILES in admin-tags.js (a frontend test checks the list matches the directory).

  3. Write the text in place, as plain English. The configuration page is not translated: it has no locale keys and does not use JE.t (A.fmt(text, params) fills {name} placeholders and {n|one|many} plural words).

docs.title: Field declarations
docs.text:
Keep each field on one line starting { id: '…', key: '…', type: '…' with a label: '…': scripts/generate_config_flag_groups.py and Services/WhatsNewService.cs read them lexically, and a frontend test enforces the shape.

Property Meaning id The control's DOM id. When a control moves here from configPage.html, keep its old id so What's New and the analytics map keep tracking it; a new id appears in What's New as a new setting, listed under Media Tags with a link to the section's tab (and group). key The PluginConfiguration property it reads and writes (PascalCase). type switch, select, number, text, textarea, pills, ordered (a checkbox in a reorderable list; orderKey, defaultOrder), enable (a Groups row switch) or custom (drawn by the section's render, declared only for tracking). label, desc The text shown, in English. options [[value, label]] for select and pills. min, max, fallback, unit Numbers are clamped and fall back when empty. secret A text field drawn as a password input (autocomplete="new-password"), for a key the server keeps private (public configuration, logs and exports never carry it). read(raw, config), write(value, config) Convert between the stored value and the control. onChange(value, config) Return more fields to write at the same time. when(config), visible(config) Disable or hide the control unless true. place: 'section' The section draws the control itself with A.fieldHtml(f, config); the tab still binds it. break: true Start a new box before this field. master: true A switch that the card's other settings depend on: drawn as the page's master switch (accent tint and edge). more: '<title>' Fields sharing it sit under one closed disclosure with that title, after the card's other fields (Quality's Display behaviour and Audio language defaults). hideWhenOff: true With when, hide the row (not only disable it) while when is false, as the page's dependent settings do.

A section with note: true (an explanation with nothing to set) is drawn as a closed disclosure after the cards, named by noteLabel (or title). A card with no scope of its own in SECTION_SCOPES marks each per-user setting with the configuration page's people icon; shared settings carry no marker.

A section whose own editors write fields that are not declared as above (the layout editor's profiles, order and caps; the Tag Styles document and preset; excluded library ids; the clear-cache signal) names them on one line: writes: ['TagLayouts', 'TagGroupOrder', 'TagGroupCaps'],.

These declarations are the tab's whole field list. JE.adminTags.pageFields() collects them and the tab refuses to save anything else; Helpers/MediaTagsPageFields.cs reads the same declarations from the embedded modules, and POST /JellyfinEnhanced/admin/configuration answers 400 for any other field, so API keys and the rest of the configuration stay with the configuration page's form. The server also checks each value against the field's contract (MediaTagsPageFields.TryNormalize, built on the normalisers the server already uses for these fields), so a value the page's controls cannot produce is refused with the reason; give a new field a case there when it has a range or a set of values. A set of values goes through OneOf, which also requires the canonical value to be in the set: several normalisers answer an empty string for a value they do not know, so without that check an empty value would pass. tests/fixtures/admin-tags-page-fields.json is the expected list; a frontend and a backend test compare both sides with it, so a new field means a declaration and a line there.

docs.title: Porting a control from the configuration page's form
docs.text:
1. Declare the field in the section that owns it, with the old id, and add its key to tests/fixtures/admin-tags-page-fields.json.
  2. Delete its markup, load/save lines, PARENT_DEPS entry and any helper from the form in configPage.html (and its schema entry in Configuration/admin/sections.js). buildConfigFromForm starts from the saved configuration, so a field the form no longer touches keeps its value.
  3. Run python3 scripts/generate_config_flag_groups.py and python3 tests/inventory/generate.py; commit the regenerated files.
  4. Add the field's behaviour to the appropriate tests/frontend/features/features-admin-tags-page-*.test.mjs concern file (the Groups file exercises every declared field automatically).

docs.title: Integrated Tier 2 controls
docs.text:
The configuration page's form contains only the Media Tags summary card on the Display tab. Its legacy section links open the matching section of the Media Tags tab. Every moved field keeps its control id and is covered by the independent binding map derived from the form at 058f982b.

Section Ported fields and validation Layout defaults TagScale (smaller/default/larger/largest), TagGap (tight/default/roomy), TagEdgeSpacing (default/tight/flush), using TagLayoutRules Groups → Awards AwardsTagsEnabled, AwardsTagsPosition, the five ribbon switches, AwardsTagsImdbList, AwardsTagsLetterboxdList (numeric id or owner/slug via AwardTagsService.IsListId) and AwardsTagsRefreshHours (1–168) Groups → Logos LogoTagsEnabled, LogoTagsPosition, LogoTagsMovieMode (provider/studio/off), LogoTagsSeriesMode (network/provider/off), LogoTagsRegion (empty follows server, otherwise a valid two-letter code) and LogoTagsMaxLogos (1–2), using LogoTagRules and WatchProvidersBatch Groups → Custom CustomTagsEnabled, CustomTagsPosition, CustomTagRules: the existing Match/Value/Label/Icon table, existing tag/collection suggestions, 20 rows, reserved-label hints and CustomTagRuleSet validation. Incomplete local rows are kept in the editor; complete valid rows auto-save. CustomTagRuleKey and CustomTagRuleSources are never declared or patchable. Colours Integrated Poster preset and its worst-case contrast badge, plus Awards/Logos/Custom targets; custom label targets follow table edits. Genre: one target per genre label (TagStyleCatalog.Labels("genre"), from js/tags/genre-icons.json) drawn as an icon tile from the catalog's genreIcons, with its name beside it above 640 px; above twelve labels the #tagStyleTargetFilter box narrows the tiles by name (Whole group and the label being edited always stay). Every group's target strip is a radiogroup with one tab stop (the selected tile, which keeps focus when the strip is rebuilt); arrow keys move the selection over the visible tiles, Home/End to the ends, and the filter box is a separate tab stop. The contrast badge rates each genre on its own. No new field: genre colours live in TagStyleOverrides (labels["genre:<genre>"]), validated by TagStyleSet.TryValidate as before, so the allowlist and validators are unchanged. The editor serializes the document in the server's stored order and keeps the group and label being edited when the page loads the stored value again Groups → Language The pre-existing priority string, strict policy and regional merging fields remain here. Personal priority arrays and native date context remain user settings. Status badges Existing family switches and day windows, plus the TMDB dependency note; no user-only date-context field is added to the patch allowlist. Status badges → families (Tier 3) StatusTagsLeaving, StatusTagsDirectPlay (switches, starting values for new users) Status badges → Leaving soon (Tier 3) No field of its own: the section shows the state from GET admin/leaving-soon (and the home row's state) with a Refresh now button that calls POST admin/leaving-soon/refresh, and links to the Services tab's Maintainerr card, which owns LeavingSoonMaintainerrUrl, LeavingSoonMaintainerrApiKey, LeavingSoonCollections, LeavingSoonRefreshHours, LeavingSoonMaintainerrActions and LeavingSoonHomeRow (saved by the configuration page, validated by LeavingSoonService.NormalizeSource). Server → Import & export Writes no field of its own: an imported server document (GET admin/media-tags/export, POST admin/media-tags/preview, Helpers/MediaTagsPortable.cs) is applied through ctx.setMany and the field patch, so every field keeps its allowlist entry, validator and conflict check. Signals (ClearLocalStorageTimestamp) and secrets are never exported or imported. Export saves pending edits first; while a save fails or waits for the conflict choice, the export dialog offers no document and says why, so it never hands out the stored settings in place of the ones on the page. Import does the same before it asks for the preview, then reads the configuration again into the page (the server compares the document with the stored settings, so they must be the ones the page shows, including fields another administrator saved or cleared since the page loaded: the configuration API omits null values, so a page field missing from a full configuration read is taken as null unless it has an edit not saved yet), and settles again before Apply; each listed change is then written with the value the preview compared as Expected (ctx.setMany(values, { base })), even when the page's copy already equals the new value, and Undo restores the preview's from values; if a field the document sets was edited on the page after the preview, Apply shows the preview again instead of writing. Server → Presets for users TagOfferedPresets (custom): a JSON array of at most 20 presets, each checked with the user import validators, at most 80 KiB of UTF-8 in its canonical stored form (MediaTagsPortable.TryNormalizeOfferedPresets); presets are checked through POST user-settings/{id}/media-tags/preview before they are offered. Rules → Default tag look rules TagLookRules (custom, section rules in sections/rules.js): the list (switch, Edit, reorder, delete with undo), the add/edit form with one to five condition rows (JE.core.tagLook.MAX_CONDITIONS; libraries from Library/VirtualFolders by name, genres and age ratings from Items/Filters), and Edit as JSON. A new rule gets its id from JE.core.tagLook.newRuleId; Save rule finds the edited rule by id (by place for an id-less rule) and keeps Enabled, ColourPreset, Slots and Shapes. The JSON box keeps a typed draft (load skips a dirty draft and shows the stale note); Revert forces the load. The server's TagLookSettings.NormalizeRules checks every save. Rules → Server-wide item looks TagLookItemOverrides (writes, section item-looks in sections/rules.js): the per-item looks the item editor's For everyone saves (JE.core.tagLook.saveItemOverride, the field patch with the list read before as Expected, once more after a 409). The section lists them with titles, Edit opens the item editor in its server mode (JE.tagItemEditor.open(id, { mode: 'server', onSave }), which hands the look back to ctx.set) and the bin removes one with Undo. MediaTagsPageFields.TryNormalize refuses more than 500 entries and any entry TagLookValidation.NormalizeItemOverrides would drop or merge (a bad id, an unknown layout or density, an id used twice), and stores the normalized list (an empty one as null). It is part of the server export and import. A new field, not a port: no configPage.html control or old-form binding existed.

All nine poster groups share the layout editor and preview. Page-wide Tag Styles, including Poster variables, skip scoped previews. The page seeds size/gap/edge and new-group defaults without changing the signed-in user's document. The current cache schema (CurrentCacheSchemaVersion in Services/TagCacheService.cs) and the resolver, renderer and pixel versions are unchanged by the admin page.

docs.title: Quality stream display fields
docs.text:
The existing sections/quality.js declares QualityAudioDisplayMode, QualityVideoCodecDisplayMode, QualityHdrDisplayMode, QualityMinimumResolution and QualityHideSdr. They appear below the category list in Groups → Quality. The three modes accept highest/all; the threshold accepts off/720p/1080p/4k, and Hide SDR is Boolean. QualityDisplayRules supplies shared read-time/user-save normalization; the patch validators reject unrecognized choices. The Quality group’s Follow server settings button restores all 23 nullable Quality overrides, including these five fields and the technical includes/orders. Explicit choices remain personal even when they equal the server defaults. These fields are present in the admin fixture and independent binding map and seed the preview's new-user document. All and visibility filtering also affect the live sample chips.

Technical additions live in the existing Quality and Status badges section modules: ShowRuntimeTag/RuntimeTagOrder, ShowAspectRatioTag/AspectRatioTagOrder, ShowFrameRateTag/FrameRateTagOrder, ShowVersionsTag/VersionsTagOrder, and StatusTagsScenes. Switches default off, order defaults are 8–11, booleans and 1–99 order values are validated by MediaTagsPageFields, and the fixture plus binding map cover the declarations. The main configuration form gains no controls. SDH is a derived subtitle fact and needs no admin field.

The portable user document carries 89 personal fields. The administrator allowlist has 115 fields including TagOfferedPresets and TagLookItemOverrides; its export contains 114 settings, excluding the clear-cache signal. The 8 MiB patch ceiling includes changes, expected values and JSON escaping, with headroom for 500 fully populated item looks and their previous values. Item look edits, removes and entry Undo capture per-id intent and Expected stamps when the user acts; save responses rebase only that pending delta. Canceled edits need no PATCH only when no write was started or the server definitively rejected it (a conflict, or a 4xx body naming the field). Network failures, 5xx responses and lost responses have unknown write outcomes: retained entry intent must be acknowledged by a successful PATCH before the page reports saved, including Undo queued during the failed save. Mutations affect at most 500 IDs; imports and import Undo explicitly replace the whole list as an array/null with whole-field Expected, bounded by the 500-entry final-list cap and the 8 MiB envelope. Until a replacement is acknowledged, entry edits and removals fold into its pending list and Retry sends that whole replacement. Keep mine / Take theirs resolves the whole replacement on conflict. Only successful acknowledgement releases replacement mode for subsequent per-entry edits.

LeavingSoonMaintainerrApiKey is explicitly excluded from both user and administrator portable exports/imports, public/private configuration and runtime snapshots, and is no field of this page (the Services tab saves it); the administrator-only core Jellyfin plugin configuration API keeps its normal credential-editing contract. Source URLs, collection names and cadence are administrator settings; private collection provenance never reaches tag clients.

docs.title: Where to show and the settings matrix
docs.text: Every group row on the Groups tab draws the same Where to show block from admin-tags.js (scopesHtml), not from its section. Rating binds its switches to RatingTagsOn…. The other groups write TagGroupScopes, which stores only the switches turned off; each group section declares writes: ['TagGroupScopes']. A group row gets Edit only when it has settings of its own (hasOwnControls). Otherwise its notes and links sit in the row: People Tags, for example, explains why it has no switches. The common controls every group offers on the admin page, the personal hub and the item editor are declared once in JE.core.tagSettingsMatrix (core/tag-renderer-base.js). The surfaces render from that declaration, and tests/browser/settings-matrix.spec.cjs checks them against it.

docs.title: Jellyfin Enhanced's API
docs.text:
Use Jellyfin Enhanced (JE)'s API to manage bookmarks, reviews, and personal settings, retrieve metadata, and work with integrations through HTTP(S) requests. Install and enable the plugin on your server first.

To use these APIs from a custom Jellyfin client, you need an HTTP client and a Jellyfin credential. You do not need the injected JE scripts.

This reference covers the 207 method/path entries in plugin version 12.14.0.0. Use the endpoint tables to check access requirements, inputs, responses, and limits.

Paths in endpoint tables are relative to /JellyfinEnhanced/. Braces mark path parameters; replace them before making a request. The catch-all routes serve only the resources described below.

Which IDs to use

Reviews use author + media type + TMDB key as their identity. Bookmarks use bookmark IDs and contain a Jellyfin item ID, with optional TMDB/TVDB metadata.

Seerr request, issue, user, and service IDs belong to Seerr; they are not Jellyfin GUIDs or TMDB IDs.

docs.title: Series and season quality summaries
docs.text:
SeriesQualityAggregation is an administrator default and per-user settings.json preference. Its fixed values are representative (default), latest, best, shared and mixed; unknown values normalize to representative. Null personal values inherit the admin default. The public configuration includes the normalized default; new-user seeding and resetting all users copy it.

Series and Season entries in GET /JellyfinEnhanced/tag-cache/{userId} and items in POST /JellyfinEnhanced/tag-data/{userId} include QualitySummary:

{
  "EpisodeCount": 2,
  "Categories": {
    "resolution": { "Best": "4K", "Latest": "1080p", "Values": ["1080p", "4K"], "AllAgree": false },
    "source": { "Best": "BluRay", "Latest": "WEB", "Values": ["WEB", "BluRay"], "AllAgree": false },
    "dynamicRange": { "Best": "HDR10", "Latest": null, "Values": [null, "HDR10"], "AllAgree": false },
    "videoCodec": { "Best": "HEVC", "Latest": "H264", "Values": ["H264", "HEVC"], "AllAgree": false },
    "audioInfo": { "Best": "ATMOS 7.1", "Latest": "DTS 5.1", "Values": ["DTS 5.1", "ATMOS 7.1"], "AllAgree": false }
  },
  "AudioByLanguage": {},
  "AudioRegionFallback": {},
  "LatestExtras": []
}

Each category keeps at most four distinct values (including null for missing metadata). Best, Latest and AllAgree are computed over every episode independently of that bound. AudioByLanguage maps available track language codes and base-language fallbacks to audio category facts; clients select exact-region matches first, then AudioRegionFallback (generic tracks for an unavailable region), then the base language and Categories.audioInfo. Categories.source summarises every version's source of every episode (ranked by copy quality: REMUX, BluRay, WEB, HD DVD, HDTV, DVD, SDTV, VHS, then SCR, TC, TS, CAM). LatestExtras contains edition and special-format labels for the newest probed aired non-virtual episode. Unknown/future air dates cannot supply latest values.

The current persisted cache schema includes the summary and server-only QualityEpisodeIds. Contributor IDs never appear in either response. Access filtering rebuilds summaries from visible contributors and replaces representative streams when necessary; the existing filterRevision changes when visibility changes. Spoiler Guard removes the summary whenever it removes quality streams. Missing summaries support legacy representative fallback. Collections are unchanged.

docs.title: Quick Start: Normal User vs Admin
docs.text:
Start here to set up your URL and credential. Use a user token for personal data or administrator credentials for admin routes.

Set one base URL, including any Jellyfin or reverse-proxy base path and without a trailing slash:

JELLYFIN_URL='https://jellyfin.example.com/jellyfin'
JE_URL="$JELLYFIN_URL/JellyfinEnhanced"
TOKEN='YOUR_JELLYFIN_ACCESS_TOKEN_OR_API_KEY'
USER_ID='9285e8b54149414941494edb9e464dcd'

Every authenticated example uses the same header:

curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" "$JE_URL/version"

Jellyfin 12 and legacy authorization headers

Use Authorization: MediaBrowser Token="…" on both Jellyfin 12 and 10.11. Acceptance of legacy headers such as X-Emby-Token and X-Emby-Authorization is controlled by Jellyfin Server. Jellyfin 12 disables legacy authorization by default. JE does not require different header names for different features.

Install the JE artifact built for your Jellyfin version; shared controller source does not guarantee identical host serialization.

docs.title: As a normal user
docs.text:
Log in as the user whose personal data you want to manage. Jellyfin's own POST /Users/AuthenticateByName returns AccessToken and a User object containing the user's Id. Supply client identification for this pre-login request:

curl -X POST "$JELLYFIN_URL/Users/AuthenticateByName" \
  -H 'Authorization: MediaBrowser Client="MyApp", Device="MyApp", DeviceId="my-app-1", Version="1.0.0"' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"Username":"YOUR_USERNAME","Pw":"YOUR_PASSWORD"}'

Use the returned access token as TOKEN. You can manage your bookmarks and reviews, and read other authors' reviews that are visible to you. Caller-scoped actions always use the identity in your token.

docs.title: As an administrator
docs.text:
A Jellyfin administrator token or server API key can call administrator routes. Use explicit target-user routes to manage another user's bookmarks, documents, or reviews.

A server API key grants administrator authority but may lack an existing user identity. It does not impersonate a user for Seerr, Activity, or caller-scoped writes.

Use a consistent lowercase, 32-character hexadecimal GUID without dashes (N format) for user IDs. You can obtain a target user's ID from Jellyfin's user API or the userId in that user's dashboard profile URL.

Ordinary document routes also accept parseable dashed GUIDs and normalize them; admin review and dedicated admin Hidden Content routes require N format.

docs.title: Authentication and identity
docs.text:
Use the access label in each endpoint table to check which credential you need. Some routes also require an existing user account or a linked Seerr identity.

Access label Effective requirement Anonymous No JE authorization attribute. A reverse proxy can impose its own access rules. Authenticated Jellyfin accepts the credential; no additional caller-account check unless stated. Own/admin Target is the token's user, or the principal has the Administrator role. Malformed document user IDs return 400; cross-user denial returns 403. An empty GUID falls back to the caller. Caller Uses the token's Jellyfin-UserId claim; there is no target-user override. Most writes require a nonempty ID. Administrator The principal has the Administrator role, or its resolved Jellyfin account has administrator permission. Seerr-linked Authenticated caller with a parseable user-ID claim and a linked Seerr identity, plus the stated permissions and setup. Account checks by route
  • Bootstrap requires only a parseable user-ID claim, even an empty GUID; it does not verify an existing account.
  • Self review writes require a nonempty claim, but do not require account lookup before saving.
  • Activity and calendar user-data resolve an existing account.
  • Catch Up resolves an existing account when recording is enabled.
  • Spoiler Guard enable actions resolve the caller and check library access.
  • Own/admin tag and statistics routes additionally resolve the target account (404 if absent).

Per-user document authorization uses the role check, rather than the broader administrator-account check used by most admin actions. No JE controller action declares a RequiresElevation policy. X-Jellyfin-User-Id does not supply caller identity or select a Seerr user.

docs.title: Response conventions
docs.text:
Check the HTTP status before reading a response body. The notes below cover request content types, field names, and error formats.

Send Content-Type: application/json for JSON bodies. Form endpoints specify their own content type. Successful JSON responses normally use 200; exceptions include Catch Up (204), starting the Spoiler Guard task (202), and conditional reads (304, no body).

Examples use the field names declared by JE: document models use PascalCase; explicit envelopes usually use camelCase. Jellyfin's output formatter can affect wire casing and omit null model properties. Handle optional values as either missing or null; do not rely on universal null omission.

Typed request binding accepts property names case-insensitively. Bodies inspected as JsonElement, including Seerr requests and usage tracking, use the exact property names shown.

Invalid JSON or parameter types can fail MVC model binding with 400 before an action runs. Missing/invalid credentials normally produce 401, and permission failures 403.

Error bodies vary: some are strings, some have message, some have success:false, and proxy errors can include code. Inspect status before parsing a success schema. 499 indicates a canceled GET after the client disconnected.

docs.title: Check version
docs.text:
GET /JellyfinEnhanced/version is anonymous. It returns unquoted text such as 12.12.0.0, or unknown if the plugin instance is unavailable.

curl "$JE_URL/version"

docs.title: Bookmarks API
docs.text:
Use these routes to bookmark a playback position and build a personal bookmarks screen. They use own/admin authorization, and do not check the client feature toggle, a TMDB API key, or a nonempty TMDB ID.

Setting Default What it does Enable Bookmarks Feature true BookmarksEnabled; enables the web client feature.

docs.title: Bookmarks Storage Directory
docs.text:
Each user's file is stored at:

{PluginsPath}/configurations/Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced/{userIdN}/bookmark.json

PluginsPath is Jellyfin's configured plugins directory, commonly {JELLYFIN_DATA_DIR}/plugins. The user folder is a lowercase N-format GUID. The filename is bookmark.json, singular.

The dictionary key is the bookmark ID. This is a complete example of one entry:

{
  "Bookmarks": {
    "Bm_1767441600000_a1b2c3d4e": {
      "ItemId": "9285e8b54149414941494edb9e464dcd",
      "TmdbId": "603",
      "TvdbId": "",
      "MediaType": "movie",
      "Name": "The Matrix",
      "Timestamp": 123.45,
      "Label": "Favorite scene",
      "CreatedAt": "2026-01-03T12:00:00.000Z",
      "UpdatedAt": "2026-01-03T12:00:00.000Z",
      "SyncedFrom": "",
      "SeasonNumber": null,
      "EpisodeNumber": null
    }
  }
}
Field Type/default Meaning ItemId String, "" Jellyfin item ID; required and nonblank for add. TmdbId, TvdbId Strings, "" Optional provider metadata. MediaType String, "" Client convention: movie or tv; the server does not enforce these values. Name, Label Strings, "" Item name and bookmark label. Timestamp Number, 0 Playback position in seconds. CreatedAt, UpdatedAt Strings, "" UTC ISO timestamps; generated by add. SyncedFrom String, "" Source item ID when copying a bookmark. SeasonNumber, EpisodeNumber Nullable integers, null Episode identity for matching replacement items.

For episode bookmarks, JE's client prefers the parent series' TMDB ID and the episode's own TVDB ID, falling back to the series' TVDB ID. The API accepts the metadata you send; it does not look these IDs up.

docs.title: Bookmarks API endpoints
docs.text:
Use add/remove for individual bookmarks. Use the document routes to read or replace the complete set.

Method Path Access Request → response GET user-settings/{userId}/bookmark.json Own/admin No body → bookmark document; missing/unreadable file gives {"Bookmarks":{}}. POST user-settings/{userId}/bookmark.json Own/admin Complete document → {"success":true,"file":"bookmark.json"}. POST user-settings/{userId}/bookmark.json/add Own/admin One entry, excluding timestamps → {"success":true,"id":"Bm_…"}. DELETE user-settings/{userId}/bookmark.json/{bookmarkId} Own/admin Bookmark dictionary key → {"success":true,"removed":true}.

Add accepts all entry fields except CreatedAt and UpdatedAt; lowercased equivalents such as itemId, seasonNumber, and episodeNumber also bind. Only a nonblank ItemId is required at action level.

Add does not validate library access, provider IDs, media type, season existence, or timestamp range.

Omitted strings default to ""; optional null strings are normalized to "". Every add generates a distinct ID, even for identical data.

curl -X POST "$JE_URL/user-settings/$USER_ID/bookmark.json/add" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"itemId":"9285e8b54149414941494edb9e464dcd","tmdbId":"603","mediaType":"movie","name":"The Matrix","timestamp":123.45,"label":"Favorite scene"}'

curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  "$JE_URL/user-settings/$USER_ID/bookmark.json"

BOOKMARK_ID='ID_RETURNED_BY_ADD'
curl -X DELETE -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  "$JE_URL/user-settings/$USER_ID/bookmark.json/$BOOKMARK_ID"

Missing removal returns 404:

{"success":false,"removed":false,"message":"No matching bookmark to remove."}

Missing ItemId on add returns 400:

{"success":false,"message":"ItemId is required."}

Add/remove use locked, strict read-modify-write operations. Corruption triggers preservation/recovery handling and a 500 error, such as:

{"success":false,"message":"Failed to add bookmark."}

Replacing the document

Whole-document POST replaces all bookmarks and can overwrite changes made since your GET. It does not strict-read the previous file. Prefer add/remove for individual changes. A lenient GET returning an empty document does not prove the disk file was healthy.

docs.title: Reviews API
docs.text:
Build star ratings or written reviews shared according to author visibility settings. One server-wide file holds every item's reviews:

{PluginsPath}/configurations/Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced/reviews.json

The store key is {userIdN}:{mediaType}:{tmdbKey}. These are local user reviews; TMDB reviews use the separate TMDB proxy.

Setting Default What it does Enable User Written Reviews false ShowUserReviews; shows the web review panel, without gating these routes. Show TMDB Reviews false ShowReviews; separate external review panel, requiring TMDB configuration. Hide reviews from hidden users true HideReviewsFromHiddenUsers; filters authors for non-admin readers. Hide reviews from disabled users true HideReviewsFromDisabledUsers; filters authors for non-admin readers. Also save review star ratings as the user's Jellyfin rating false MirrorReviewRatingsToJellyfin; optional rating mirroring described below. Show average user rating on poster cards false ShowUserRatingOnPosters; governs poster/tag-cache inclusion, without gating reviews/ratings.

Existing authors always see their own reviews. Administrators bypass author filtering, including deleted/orphaned authors. Non-admin readers see orphaned reviews only when both author filters are disabled; the stored ID can then be the display name. The direct review API applies author visibility; Spoiler Guard's client review hiding is a separate presentation rule.

docs.title: Rating and content rules
docs.text:
You can submit text, stars, or both. All self/admin POSTs accept the same body:

Property Type Validation content Optional string Trimmed; at most 2000 characters after trimming. Missing/null becomes "". rating Optional nullable number 1..5, in 0.5 increments; missing/null means no stars.

Empty/whitespace text with no rating returns 400 {"success":false,"message":"A rating or review text is required."}. Invalid ratings return 400 with message:"Rating must be between 1 and 5, in 0.5 increments.".

Upsert replaces text and rating and preserves the original createdAt; omitting either clears that field rather than preserving it.

docs.title: Reviewing a season or episode of a TV show
docs.text:
Use an extended TMDB key to identify a season or episode separately from the whole title.

mediaType must be exactly movie or tv. The independent tmdbId key accepts ^\d+(:s\d+(:e\d+)?)?$:

Key Intended use 1399 Whole title 1399:s1 Season 1399:s1:e1 Episode

No positive-ID or season/episode-existence check runs. Leading zeros are retained.

Extended keys are accepted for either media type: reviews/movie/603:s1 passes validation; reviews/movie:s1/603 returns a media-type error; reviews/movie/603:s returns Invalid TmdbId.. Use consistent keys and URL-encode colons if needed.

docs.title: Get reviews for an item
docs.text:
Read an item's visible reviews, or fetch rating aggregates for a batch of keys.

Method Path Access Response GET reviews/{mediaType}/{tmdbId} Authenticated {"reviews":[<review>]}; empty array when no visible review exists. GET reviews/ratings Authenticated Query keys; visible rated-review aggregates. 
curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" "$JE_URL/reviews/movie/603"
curl -G -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  --data-urlencode 'keys=movie:603,tv:1399:s1' "$JE_URL/reviews/ratings"

A review has this shape:

{
  "userId": "9285e8b54149414941494edb9e464dcd",
  "userName": "alice",
  "tmdbId": "603",
  "mediaType": "movie",
  "content": "Great movie!",
  "rating": 4.5,
  "createdAt": "2026-01-03T12:00:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-01-05T09:30:00.000Z"
}

Text-only reviews have a missing or null rating; rating-only reviews have content:"". The per-item response contains no aggregate fields.

The batch route accepts comma-separated mediaType:tmdbKey values. It ignores malformed entries and collapses duplicates. No valid keys or more than 200 distinct valid keys returns 400.

{"ratings":{"movie:603":{"average":4.5,"count":2},"tv:1399:s1":null}}

count counts visible reviews with a nonzero, non-NaN rating, rather than all written reviews. null means no visible rated review. The direct aggregate route has no display-toggle gate.

docs.title: Write and delete reviews
docs.text:
Use the caller routes for your own reviews. As an administrator, use the explicit author routes to write or delete another author's review.

Method Path Access Response POST reviews/{mediaType}/{tmdbId} Caller, nonempty ID Review body → {"success":true}. DELETE reviews/{mediaType}/{tmdbId} Caller, nonempty ID {"success":true}, even when no review existed. POST reviews/admin/{userIdN}/{mediaType}/{tmdbId} Administrator Review body → {"success":true}. DELETE reviews/admin/{userIdN}/{mediaType}/{tmdbId} Administrator {"success":true,"removed":true}, or 404 below. GET reviews/admin/all Administrator Filtered/paged export described below. 
curl -X POST "$JE_URL/reviews/tv/1399:s1:e1" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"rating":4.5}'

curl -X POST "$JE_URL/reviews/admin/$USER_ID/movie/603" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"content":"Great movie!","rating":5}'

Admin author IDs must parse as N-format GUIDs, but the account need not exist and the supplied ID string is retained in the store key. Use canonical lowercase IDs to avoid casing-dependent duplicates. Missing admin deletion returns:

{"success":false,"removed":false,"message":"No matching review to delete."}

With rating mirroring enabled, whole-movie/series stars are written to an accessible matching Jellyfin item as stars × 2. New stars overwrite its previous Jellyfin rating.

Removing stars or deleting a review clears that rating only if it still matches the previous mirrored value within 0.01. Season/episode keys are excluded. Missing accounts/items or mirror failures do not undo the review operation.

docs.title: Admin export and polling
docs.text:
Use reviews/admin/all to export reviews or poll for updates. The filters and pagination rules below apply to this administrator route.

Query Default Rules since Unset Parseable ISO 8601; inclusive updatedAt >= since; invalid value returns 400. userId Unset One N-format author ID; invalid value returns 400. limit 500 1..1000; out-of-range returns 400. offset 0 Nonnegative; negative returns 400. 
curl -G -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  --data-urlencode 'since=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z' \
  --data-urlencode 'limit=100' --data-urlencode 'offset=0' "$JE_URL/reviews/admin/all"

Response: {"reviews":[<review>],"total":1,"offset":0,"limit":100}. total counts all matching rows.

Results sort by updatedAt ascending (oldest matching reviews first), then store key in ordinal order. Unparseable update timestamps are included regardless of since and sort first. Admin exports bypass author filters.

De-duplicate polling results by author + media type + TMDB key because since is inclusive. Pagination is not a snapshot; changes during paging can move rows. There is no deletion/tombstone stream.

Reads are lenient and may return an empty store after corruption/I/O failure. Mutations strict-read the shared store, refuse to overwrite unreadable data, attempt a .corrupt-<timestamp> backup copy, and return 500 on failure. For example: {"success":false,"message":"Failed to save review."}.

docs.title: Per-User Settings Files
docs.text:
Use these routes to read or replace a user's saved preferences and state. They provide six explicit typed document pairs; unknown properties do not become arbitrary stored data.

All use own/admin authorization. GETs are no-store; POST replaces the complete document and normally returns {"success":true,"file":"<filename>"}. These routes are not an arbitrary file service.

Method Path Document GET user-settings/{userId}/settings.json Enhanced settings POST user-settings/{userId}/settings.json Replace Enhanced settings GET user-settings/{userId}/shortcuts.json Shortcut list POST user-settings/{userId}/shortcuts.json Replace shortcut list GET user-settings/{userId}/elsewhere.json Provider preferences POST user-settings/{userId}/elsewhere.json Replace provider preferences GET user-settings/{userId}/ddd-triggers.json Picked DoesTheDogDie trigger IDs, {Triggers:[int]} POST user-settings/{userId}/ddd-triggers.json Replace picked trigger IDs GET user-settings/{userId}/hidden-content.json Hidden Content state POST user-settings/{userId}/hidden-content.json Replace Hidden Content state GET user-settings/{userId}/spoilerblur.json Raw Spoiler Guard state POST user-settings/{userId}/spoilerblur.json Replace raw Spoiler Guard state

The bookmark GET/POST pair is listed in Bookmarks API endpoints. All documents live in the same user directory. Save failures generally return 500 {"success":false,"message":"…"}.

Settings, shortcuts, Elsewhere, and bookmark whole-file saves do not strict-read the previous document.

The Hidden Content and shortcuts GETs, and the same two documents in bootstrap, never answer an empty document for a stored file they cannot read, because clients save both whole. A read error returns 500 (in bootstrap, the document is null, which Jellyfin's serializer leaves out of UserSettings) and leaves the file as it is. Content that does not parse is first moved aside to .corrupt-<timestamp>, as a save would, so the next read returns the defaults.

Hidden Content and raw Spoiler Guard saves lock and strict-read first: corruption returns 503 with backup/retry guidance, temporary I/O failures 500.

Raw Spoiler Guard POST has a 2 MiB request limit and at most 1000 entries in each of Series, Movies, Collections, PendingTmdb; exceeding the dictionary cap returns 413.

It maintains pending-promotion registrations. Its GET is lenient and can return defaults for corrupt data; caller-facing Spoiler Guard reads instead report corruption.

curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  "$JE_URL/user-settings/$USER_ID/settings.json"

curl -X POST "$JE_URL/user-settings/$USER_ID/elsewhere.json" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"Region":"US","Regions":["US"],"Services":[],"SeasonProviders":true}'

docs.title: Settings document
docs.text:
GET can create a first settings file using saved administrator defaults. It adds IsAdmin, computed for the caller, even when reading another user's document. POST ignores that derived field. POST normalizes the tag layout fields before saving: an unknown layout or density falls back to corners / full, unknown groups and slots are dropped, caps are clamped to 0–10 and the group order is deduplicated.

Read the current document, modify the needed properties, and send it back to preserve other preferences.

The table below gives the UserSettings model defaults used when properties are omitted in a replacement body. They differ from initial values seeded by saved server configuration. For example, first GET seeds LastOpenedTab:"shortcuts", and server defaults can enable features whose model defaults are false. See settings overview for the settings workflow.

Optional fields inherit the default look. Unknown layouts/densities become null, invalid groups/slots are dropped, caps clamp to 0–10. Caps ({Quality,…,Custom}, 0–10, null per group keeps the user's), TagScale, TagGap and EdgeSpacing are optional (null keeps the user's; unknown values are stored as null); Scope is "item" (a Series lock stays on the series card) or null (its seasons and episodes inherit it). Written by the item editor (tags/tag-item-editor.js) null ShowRatingInPlayer Boolean true RemoveContinueWatchingEnabled Boolean false LastOpenedTab String "" ReviewsExpandedByDefault Boolean false DisplayLanguage String "" CalendarDisplayMode String "list" CalendarDefaultViewMode String "agenda"

Shapes on rules and locks uses the same {Landscape,List} map as TagShapeOverrides; it layers over that rule's or lock's look, independently of the user's shape overrides. Resolution is the user's lock → the administrator's item look (TagLookItemOverrides) → first matching rule → shape override → default; a lock or item look on the item itself comes before one on its series (core/tag-layout.js lookSource, and natively PosterTagSettings.ForItem, which applies locks, item looks and rules but not shapes). POST also accepts a shape slot map such as {"quality":"bottom","status":"top"}; stored responses use arrays, matching TagLayouts and preserving group ids across key-case conversion. Layout/Density null inherits, and null caps inherit per group. A shape that changes layout uses the profile of the new layout. Portrait and square cards always use the default shape; Native Poster Tags ignore these objects.

TagScale and TagGap are presentation-only settings, normalized case-insensitively on save. An unknown global value becomes default; null inherits the administrator's validated choice, then default. Version-0 documents always render at default size/gap. Promotion writes explicit default values so changing another layout setting does not adopt new administrator sizing. New-user seeding and reset-all copy the administrator's values. A shape's optional TagScale/TagGap uses the same choices, with unknown values normalized to null (inherit). Shape fields also round-trip inside rule/lock Shapes. Native posters use global size/gap in their rendering metrics and settings digest, with shape overrides still web-only. These fields do not change TagCacheEntry or its schema.

The web client keeps these nullable fields null while they inherit: the settings panel shows the administrator's current value for ShowEditionTag, ShowLowQualitySourceTag, the three technical category switches (ShowRuntimeTag, ShowAspectRatioTag, ShowFrameRateTag), ShowVersionsTag, the three display modes, minimum resolution, Hide SDR, the eleven *TagOrder fields and SeriesQualityAggregation, and saves null for each one the user has not changed, so a save, an import or its Undo never pins today's administrator default. Inheriting is a state, not a value comparison: any change through a panel control (even back to the administrator's value), an imported value (even one equal to the default) and a reorder of the quality categories (all ten orders) are saved as the user's own. Only Follow server in the series policy, Follow server settings in the Quality group, or an import or Undo of a null value makes a field inherit again.

docs.title: Media Tags import, export and presets
docs.text:
A user's Media Tags settings travel as a versioned document with the same PascalCase field names as settings.json:

{ "v": 1, "kind": "je-media-tags-user", "settings": { "TagLayout": "bands", "TagLayoutSettingsVersion": 1, "TagScale": "larger", "QualityTagsEnabled": true } }

settings holds 89 personal Media Tags fields (MediaTagsPortable.UserFields, including the three display modes, minimum resolution, Hide SDR, technical categories and the Versions chip): the group switches (QualityTagsEnabled … CustomTagsEnabled, PeopleTagsEnabled, TagsHideOnHover, UseNativePosterTags), quality includes and orders, QualityTagsPreferredAudioLanguage, SeriesQualityAggregation, the rating scopes, sources, minimum and colour switch, TagGroupScopes (each group's personal Where to show switches), the language display and priority fields, the seven status families (including Scenes), the nine *TagsPosition fields, TagLayout, TagLayoutSettingsVersion, TagLayouts, TagGroupOrder, TagGroupCaps, TagLabelDensity, TagScale, TagGap, TagEdgeSpacing, TagShapeOverrides and TagStylePreset. Rules and locks (TagLookRules, TagLayoutLocks) are not part of it: they name the server's libraries and items. A preset is the same document with kind: "je-media-tags-preset", an id (lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, up to 40), a name (1–60 characters) and a description (up to 240); its settings may name only some fields.

Method Path Access Request → response GET user-settings/{userId}/media-tags/export Own/admin No body → the user document above, every field in UserFields order. POST user-settings/{userId}/media-tags/preview Own/admin A user document or a preset (64 KB limit) → {kind, v, name, description, imported:{Field:value}, changes:[{field, from, to}], skipped:[{field, reason, detail}]}. Nothing is saved; the client writes the changed fields through POST settings.json. 400 {error} refuses the document as a whole: not-object, kind, version (missing or not a positive integer), newer (v above the server's), settings (not an object). GET user-settings/{userId}/media-tags/presets Own/admin No body → {max:10, builtIn:[preset], offered:[preset], mine:[preset]}: the shipped presets (Assets/TagPresets/*.json), the administrator's TagOfferedPresets and the user's own. POST user-settings/{userId}/media-tags/presets Own/admin A preset, or a user document with a name (64 KB limit) → {preset, skipped}; the stored preset gets a new id and keeps only the accepted settings. 400 {error}: a document error above, name, description, empty (no usable setting) or full with max (10 per user). DELETE user-settings/{userId}/media-tags/presets/{presetId} Own/admin No body → {success:true}; 404 {error:"missing"} for an unknown id. GET admin/media-tags/export Administrator No body → {v:1, kind:"je-media-tags-admin", settings:{…}}: every field of the Media Tags tab's allowlist (MediaTagsPageFields.Allowed) in the configuration API's shape, sorted, except ClearLocalStorageTimestamp. Secrets (CustomTagRuleKey, API keys, tokens, passwords) are never included. POST admin/media-tags/preview Administrator An administrator document, or a personal export (kind: "je-media-tags-user") to make the administrator's own settings the server defaults; fields the page does not own come back in skipped (8 MiB limit, the configuration patch limit) → {kind, v, imported, changes, skipped}. Each field is read and checked exactly as POST admin/configuration reads it (PluginConfigurationPatch.TryRead); the page then applies the changes through that patch, with the values it read as Expected.

Each user field is checked on its own: it must be one of UserFields, have the property's JSON type, pass the administrator field contract where the configuration has a field of that name and type (positions, orders 1–99, known values, minimum score 0–10, text limits), and come out of the settings save path's normalisation (MediaTagsPortable.TryNormalizeUser, the same call POST settings.json makes) exactly as given. Anything else is reported in skipped and never applied: reason is unknown, invalid (with the validator's detail), secret, or for administrator documents signal. secret covers every credential field of the plugin configuration as spelled (MediaTagsPortable.Secrets: TMDB_API_KEY, the other *ApiKey fields, SonarrInstances/RadarrInstances, CustomTagRuleKey, AnalyticsInstallSecret) and any other name ending in an API key or token or containing password or secret, ignoring case, _ and -. null keeps its meaning (follow the administrator). Saved presets live in media-tag-presets.json in the user's directory, read-modify-written under the user's file lock.

The administrator's offered presets are the page field TagOfferedPresets: a JSON array text of at most 20 presets with distinct ids, each valid as a whole (no unknown or invalid setting); "" offers none. The cap is 80 KiB (81,920 UTF-8 bytes, MediaTagsPortable.MaxOfferedPresetsBytes) for the text as sent and for its canonical stored form: the presets normalised and serialised the way the server stores them, with non-ASCII and HTML-sensitive characters escaped (< becomes \u003C), which can be several times longer than the text sent. A value over the cap once normalised is refused (larger than 81920 bytes once normalised (N bytes)), so every stored value exports and imports again unchanged. POST admin/configuration (and the import preview) reads up to 8 MiB (PluginConfigurationPatch.MaxRequestBytes) for the entire JSON body, including both Changes and Expected, outer string escaping and any Tag Styles data. Individually valid fields can exceed that aggregate limit together. Such a request is refused before any write; reduce the document and retry. Imports use the existing page conflict handling: each request is atomic, but resolving conflicts can retry the non-conflicting fields separately. There is no guarantee that every maximal old/new document fits one request.

Versioning. v grows only when a field is renamed, removed or changes meaning. New fields are added without a new version: an older server reports them as unknown and applies the rest. A server refuses a document whose v is higher than its own (newer), and reads an older v through that version's migration before checking it. kind never changes for an existing document type.

docs.title: Shortcuts and Elsewhere documents
docs.text:
Use these documents to save shortcut overrides and provider preferences.

shortcuts.json defaults to {"Shortcuts":[]}. Each shortcut has string fields Name, Key, Label, Category, all defaulting to "". The JSON file holds overrides; it does not itself describe every built-in shortcut.

{"Shortcuts":[{"Name":"example","Key":"Ctrl+K","Label":"Example","Category":"custom"}]}

elsewhere.json defaults to:

{"Region":"","Regions":[],"Services":[],"SeasonProviders":true}

Region is a string, Regions and Services are string arrays, and SeasonProviders is a boolean. These routes do not call provider services or validate region/provider availability.

docs.title: Hidden Content document
docs.text:
hidden-content.json contains Items (dictionary of HiddenContentItem) and Settings. Items defaults to {}. First ordinary GET can seed Settings from saved administrator defaults. The dedicated admin GET below uses a lenient read without this seeding.

Entry field Type/default ItemId, Name, Type, TmdbId, HiddenAt, PosterPath, SeriesId, SeriesName Strings, "" SeasonNumber, EpisodeNumber Nullable integers, null HideScope String, "global"; scopes are global, continuewatching, nextup, homesections.

Model settings defaults:

{
  "Enabled": true,
  "FilterLibrary": true,
  "FilterDiscovery": true,
  "FilterUpcoming": true,
  "FilterCalendar": true,
  "FilterSearch": false,
  "FilterRecommendations": true,
  "FilterRequests": true,
  "FilterNextUp": true,
  "FilterContinueWatching": true,
  "ShowHideButtons": true,
  "ShowHideConfirmation": true,
  "ShowButtonJellyseerr": true,
  "ShowButtonLibrary": false,
  "ShowButtonDetails": true,
  "ShowButtonCast": false,
  "ExperimentalHideCollections": false
}

docs.title: Admin Hidden Content API
docs.text:
Manage other users' hidden items without replacing the whole document. These dedicated routes require administrator authority and the server toggle below. The ordinary own/admin file routes do not check this toggle.

Setting Default What it does Let admins view and manage other users' hidden content true HiddenContentAdmin; admits these dedicated admin actions. Method Path Request → response GET admin/hidden-content-users {"users":[{"userId":"…","userName":"alice","count":2}]}. GET admin/hidden-content/{userId} {"userId":"…","userName":"alice","hiddenContent":{"Items":{},"Settings":{}}}; Settings has the document fields above. POST admin/hidden-content/{userId}/hide Raw array of entries → {"success":true,"added":1}. POST admin/hidden-content/{userId}/unhide Raw array of dictionary keys → {"success":true,"removed":1}.

Target IDs must be nonempty N-format GUIDs (400 otherwise); unknown accounts return 404.

The user list includes existing accounts with stored hidden items, omits the caller and zero-count/deleted users, and sorts names case-insensitively. Lenient reads can report empty/default state for unreadable files.

curl -X POST "$JE_URL/admin/hidden-content/$USER_ID/hide" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '[{"ItemId":"9285e8b54149414941494edb9e464dcd","Name":"Example movie","Type":"Movie","HideScope":"global"}]'

curl -X POST "$JE_URL/admin/hidden-content/$USER_ID/unhide" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '["9285e8b54149414941494edb9e464dcd"]'

Hide requires a nonempty array of at most 200 entries. Entries need ItemId or TmdbId; the key is ItemId, otherwise tmdb-{TmdbId}. Empty or over-256-character keys and duplicates are skipped. Existing items are retained.

Unknown HideScope values become global; missing HiddenAt gets a server UTC timestamp.

The action truncates Name, SeriesName, PosterPath to 512 characters, SeriesId to 128, Type to 64, TmdbId to 32, and supplied HiddenAt to 64.

Unhide requires a nonempty key array; empty/over-256-character keys are ignored.

Both mutations are locked and strict-reading. Zero changes still succeeds.

Corruption returns 503 {"success":false,"message":"Hidden-content store is corrupt; backed up. Please retry."}; temporary I/O failure returns 500, as do other storage failures. These actions do not validate each supplied item's library existence.

See content management for the web workflow.

docs.title: Continue Watching / Next Up
docs.text:
These caller actions store scoped Hidden Content entries, rather than changing watched state.

Method Path Access Response POST continue-watching/hide/{itemId} Caller {"success":true,"key":"…","entry":<HiddenContentItem>}. DELETE continue-watching/hide/{itemId} Caller {"success":true}. POST next-up/hide/{itemId} Caller Same hide response. DELETE next-up/hide/{itemId} Caller Same unhide response. 
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  "$JE_URL/continue-watching/hide/9285e8b54149414941494edb9e464dcd"

POST requires an existing caller and an accessible Jellyfin item. Malformed item IDs return 400; unavailable/inaccessible items return 404.

POST seeds administrator defaults and turns filtering on only when it creates hidden-content.json. An existing file keeps its settings, including disabled filtering, even when its item list is empty.

Hiding on both surfaces widens the scope to homesections; an existing global hide stays global.

DELETE removes only the matching exact surface scope. A wider global/homesections entry can therefore yield 404 {"success":false,"message":"No matching hidden-content entry."}. Corruption returns 503; storage failures return 500. There is no target-user override.

docs.title: Seerr Integration API
docs.text:
Use the Seerr routes for discovery, requests, quotas, and issues. The route prefix remains jellyseerr even when you use Seerr. Configure the server connection in Seerr settings.

Setting Default What it does Enable Seerr integration false JellyseerrEnabled; enables integration. Seerr URL(s) (One per line) "" JellyseerrUrls; server-reachable URLs, generally tried in order. Seerr API Key "" JellyseerrApiKey; server-side upstream credential. Auto import Jellyfin users to Seerr false JellyseerrAutoImportUsers; lookup/status may import unlinked callers. Blocked Users "" JellyseerrImportBlockedUsers; excludes selected users from lookup/import. Disable server-side response cache false JellyseerrDisableCache; bypasses normal response, user, and enrichment caches. Response Cache TTL (min) 10 JellyseerrResponseCacheTtlMinutes; minimum one minute. User ID Cache TTL (min) 30 JellyseerrUserIdCacheTtlMinutes; minimum one minute. Sync Seerr Watchlist → Jellyfin false SyncJellyseerrWatchlist; required for manual watchlist sync. Add requested media to Watchlist false AddRequestedMediaToWatchlist; adds successfully requested media through the watchlist workflow.

docs.title: Caller identity, permissions, and errors
docs.text:
Check these requirements before calling a Seerr proxy. Requests use your token's identity and the permissions of your linked Seerr account.

Ordinary proxies need enabled integration, URLs, API key, and a linked authenticated caller. JE derives the caller from the token's Jellyfin-UserId claim and uses that caller's Seerr identity upstream.

User lookup/status can auto-import; permission audit never auto-imports. Supplying an extra user-ID header does not change this identity.

Operation Permission for non-admin callers Request creation, including seasons At least one of REQUEST, REQUEST_MOVIE, REQUEST_TV; Seerr validates its own media-specific rules. Advanced request fields REQUEST_ADVANCED or MANAGE_REQUESTS; otherwise JE strips serverId, profileId, rootFolder, languageProfileId, tags. Service and override-rule discovery A request permission, REQUEST_ADVANCED, or MANAGE_REQUESTS. Issue reads VIEW_ISSUES or MANAGE_ISSUES. Issue creation CREATE_ISSUES or MANAGE_ISSUES.

Jellyfin administrators and Seerr ADMIN callers bypass these permission checks, while ordinary proxy calls still require linkage.

Missing setup returns 503; missing caller claim 403; unreachable Seerr 502 with code:"unreachable"; blocked lookup 403 with code:"blocked"; unlinked reachable caller 404 with code:"unlinked". Reachability is checked before the blocked/unlinked distinction.

Permission errors include no_request_permission, no_issue_permission, and no_issue_view_permission. Upstream authentication/authorization errors can return 401/403; other upstream statuses can pass through. Admin error bodies may contain more diagnostics.

Success forwards upstream JSON, rather than a universal success envelope. Lists commonly contain results, page, totalPages, totalResults, or pageInfo; detail/service/rating bodies keep the upstream schema.

GET parental filtering can change lists or deny detail/subresource access. Request/issue validation remains Seerr's responsibility where JE does not impose a documented check.

Jellyfin parental policy applies server-side. Denied title/request access returns 403 {"error":true,"code":"parental_block","message":"This title is above your parental rating limit."}.

A title's rating is read the way Jellyfin's TMDB metadata fills an item's rating: the certification for the server's metadata country, else the US one, and for a series else the first one listed (the country's or US entry decides even when its rating is empty, which leaves the title unrated). It is scored in the server's country first, as Jellyfin scores the rating it stores, and compared with the user's limit as Jellyfin compares it: a lower score is allowed whatever its sub-score, a higher one is not, and the user's sub-score limit decides only at the limit's own score. A title with no rating follows the user's block-unrated setting.

Filtered reads still awaiting rating verification can return 504 with code:"parental_pending" and Retry-After: 2; retry these instead of treating them as an empty successful page.

GETs can return 499 on disconnect. Proxy POSTs continue independently of client disconnects.

docs.title: Status and administrative operations
docs.text:
Use these routes to check connectivity and user linkage, test connection settings, or run administrator operations such as import and watchlist sync.

Method Path Access Inputs → response GET jellyseerr/status Authenticated {"active":true}; reachability only, cached 30 seconds, including negative results. GET jellyseerr/user-status Authenticated/caller active, userFound, reason; linked results also contain string jellyseerrUserId and boolean canRequestAdvanced; no-store. GET jellyseerr/validate Administrator Query url, header X-Arr-ApiKey → {"ok":true}. POST jellyseerr/trigger-recently-added-scan Administrator Query url, header X-Arr-ApiKey, no body needed → {"ok":true}. GET jellyseerr/permission-audit Administrator Array of {jellyfinUsername,jellyfinUserId,linked,permissions,issues}. POST jellyseerr/import-users Administrator No body → {success,usersImported,totalUsers,errors}. POST jellyseerr/sync-watchlist Administrator No body → {success,itemsProcessed,itemsAdded,errors}. GET jellyseerr/settings/{type} Administrator Exact type=sonarr or radarr → upstream connection-settings array, including API keys. GET jellyseerr/settings/partial-requests Authenticated {partialRequestsEnabled,enableSpecialEpisodes} booleans, without caller linkage. GET jellyfin-urls Administrator {externalUrl,internalUrl} detected/published Jellyfin URLs. GET jellyseerr/user Administrator + Seerr-linked Optional take=1000 → upstream user roster, not the caller's profile.

User-status ordinarily returns 200 with reasons disabled, no_user, blocked, unlinked, unreachable, or linked; status does not establish linking. It can use cached user results. For example:

{"active":true,"userFound":true,"reason":"linked","jellyseerrUserId":"7","canRequestAdvanced":false}

curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" "$JE_URL/jellyseerr/user-status"

SEERR_URL='http://seerr:5055'
SEERR_KEY='YOUR_SEERR_API_KEY'
curl -G -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H "X-Arr-ApiKey: $SEERR_KEY" --data-urlencode "url=$SEERR_URL" \
  "$JE_URL/jellyseerr/validate"

Validation and manual scan test one supplied, possibly unsaved URL/key. Missing inputs or a rejected URL return 400 {ok:false,message}. Upstream failures add code and optional cfRay; connection failure returns 502.

Recently-added scan updates Seerr's library availability, rather than completing downloads/imports. Use service URLs reachable from the Jellyfin server/container; URL mappings control browser links separately.

The URL guard allows HTTP(S) and loopback, blocks metadata/unspecified addresses and literal IPv4 link-local URLs, and permits allowed container-host alias mappings.

Permission audit requires configured integration (503 otherwise), bypasses cached lookup, and returns numeric permission bits or null plus issue strings for each account.

Manual import excludes blocked users, does not require auto-import enabled, returns 400 for missing setup, and has a 30-second throttle (429). A reached import can succeed with per-user errors; total upstream failure returns 502.

Watchlist sync requires its toggle, enabled integration, and credentials (400 if missing); it uses the first URL whose user list loads, returns 502 if none does, and can succeed with per-user errors. errors is nullable/omittable when none occurred. Missing users are not imported by sync. See Seerr features for scheduled watchlist behavior.

settings/{type} backs Import from Seerr in the admin *arr tab. It uses the first configured URL and does not require caller linkage; invalid type returns 400, setup 503, upstream rejection 403 or other upstream status. Treat returned instance API keys as credentials.

Partial-request settings try configured URLs and return structured 503 with code:"disabled" or "unreachable" if unavailable.

docs.title: Seerr Discovery & Requests
docs.text:
Use these routes to browse titles, submit requests, check quotas, and work with issues.

All routes in this table require Seerr-linked access, except TV-by-studio's separately described TMDB implementation. Numeric title IDs are TMDB IDs; genre, keyword, person, collection, network, and studio IDs belong to TMDB. Service IDs belong to Seerr.

Method Path Parameters and result GET jellyseerr/search Required nonblank query, page=1 (minimum 1), optional language → upstream search page. GET jellyseerr/sonarr Request/discovery permission → upstream service list. GET jellyseerr/radarr Request/discovery permission → upstream service list. GET jellyseerr/sonarr/lookup/{tmdbId} Request/discovery permission → upstream Sonarr match candidates. GET jellyseerr/{type}/{serverId} Exact type=sonarr or radarr (400 otherwise) → service profiles/folders/details. POST jellyseerr/request JSON request object → upstream request record. GET jellyseerr/request take=500, skip=0, filter=all, forwarded without JE clamping (filter escaped as one value) → upstream request page. GET jellyseerr/quota Caller's quota; movie/TV sides can gain ISO nextResetAt. GET jellyseerr/movie/{tmdbId} Movie detail. Spoiler Guard shapes this and the other title responses for the caller; see below. GET jellyseerr/tv/{tmdbId} TV detail. GET jellyseerr/tv/{tmdbId}/season/{seasonNumber} Season detail; numeric route values forwarded. GET jellyseerr/movie-collections Query ids → collection map, described below. GET jellyseerr/movie/{tmdbId}/similar page=1 → upstream title page. GET jellyseerr/movie/{tmdbId}/recommendations page=1 → upstream title page. GET jellyseerr/movie/{tmdbId}/ratingscombined Upstream combined movie ratings. GET jellyseerr/tv/{tmdbId}/similar page=1 → upstream title page. GET jellyseerr/tv/{tmdbId}/recommendations page=1 → upstream title page. GET jellyseerr/tv/{tmdbId}/ratings Upstream TV ratings. GET jellyseerr/discover/trending page=1, discover filters → upstream discovery page. GET jellyseerr/discover/movies page=1, discover filters → upstream discovery page. GET jellyseerr/discover/tv page=1, discover filters → upstream discovery page. GET jellyseerr/discover/movies/upcoming page=1, discover filters → upstream discovery page. GET jellyseerr/discover/tv/upcoming page=1, discover filters → upstream discovery page. GET jellyseerr/discover/tv/network/{networkId} page=1, discover filters → upstream discovery page. GET jellyseerr/discover/movies/studio/{studioId} page=1, discover filters → upstream discovery page. GET jellyseerr/discover/tv/studio/{studioId} Caller + enabled Seerr + TMDB key; positive studioId, page=1 within 1..500, optional sortBy, discover filters under TMDB's names. GET jellyseerr/discover/tv/genre/{genreId} page=1, discover filters → upstream discovery page. GET jellyseerr/discover/movies/genre/{genreId} page=1, discover filters → upstream discovery page. GET jellyseerr/discover/tv/keyword/{keywordId} page=1, discover filters → upstream discovery page. GET jellyseerr/discover/movies/keyword/{keywordId} page=1, discover filters → upstream discovery page. GET jellyseerr/discover/genreslider/movie Upstream genre-slider rows. GET jellyseerr/discover/genreslider/tv Upstream genre-slider rows. GET jellyseerr/filters/languages Upstream language list, for the discovery Original language filter. GET jellyseerr/filters/certifications/{mediaType} mediaType exactly movie or tv (400 invalid_media_type otherwise) → upstream content ratings by country. GET jellyseerr/filters/watchproviders/{mediaType} mediaType exactly movie or tv; optional watchRegion, a two-letter upper-case code, defaulting to Default Region (or US); 400 invalid_media_type / invalid_region otherwise → upstream streaming services in that region. GET jellyseerr/person/{personId} Positive person ID (400 otherwise) → upstream person detail. GET jellyseerr/person/{personId}/combined_credits Positive person ID → upstream filmography. GET jellyseerr/collection/{collectionId} Upstream collection detail.
