GET jellyseerr/overrideRule Request/discovery permission → upstream override-rule list when the linked Seerr user is a Seerr admin; otherwise [] without calling Seerr, which lets only its admins read the rules and applies them itself when a request is created. POST jellyseerr/request/tv/{tmdbId}/seasons Positive TMDB route ID, request body → upstream request record. GET jellyseerr/watchlist page=1, minimum 1 → caller's upstream watchlist page; uncached. POST jellyseerr/watchlist {tmdbId, mediaType} with a positive tmdbId and mediaType of movie or tv (400 otherwise, or when Seerr or Requested media goes on the requester's watchlist is off); only those two fields are forwarded, as the caller → upstream watchlist record (409 when already on it). GET jellyseerr/issue Optional positive Seerr mediaId; take=20 clamped 1..200, skip=0 minimum 0, filter=all, sort=added → upstream issue page. GET jellyseerr/issue/{id} Positive Seerr issue ID (400 otherwise) → upstream issue detail. POST jellyseerr/issue Upstream issue JSON → upstream issue record.

Search trims long queries to at most 256 UTF-16 units without splitting a surrogate pair; blank query returns 400 with code:"missing_query". Feed/similar/recommendation pagination is generally forwarded without bounds checks; only the documented search, watchlist, and TV-studio actions clamp or validate it.

Discover routes that say “discover filters” forward nonempty query values for sortBy, primaryReleaseDateGte, primaryReleaseDateLte, firstAirDateGte, firstAirDateLte, voteAverageGte, voteAverageLte, voteCountGte, voteCountLte, withRuntimeGte, withRuntimeLte, certification, certificationGte, certificationLte, certificationCountry, watchRegion, language, genre, keywords, excludeKeywords, watchProviders. Upstream Seerr interprets these strings. On a genre or keyword route, a genre or keywords value joins the route's own with a comma (all of them). The discovery filters list their choices from the three jellyseerr/filters/… routes, tmdb/genres/{movie|tv} and tmdb/search/keyword.

curl -G -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  --data-urlencode 'query=The Matrix' --data-urlencode 'page=1' \
  "$JE_URL/jellyseerr/search"

curl -X POST "$JE_URL/jellyseerr/request" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"mediaType":"movie","mediaId":603,"is4k":false}'

curl -X POST "$JE_URL/jellyseerr/request/tv/1399/seasons" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"mediaType":"tv","mediaId":1399,"seasons":[1],"is4k":false}'

curl -X POST "$JE_URL/jellyseerr/issue" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"mediaId":42,"issueType":1,"message":"Playback problem"}'

The issue example's mediaId is a Seerr media-record ID. Nonpositive issue-list mediaId is ignored.

On the seasons route, a supplied string mediaType must equal tv case-insensitively, and a supplied numeric mediaId must match the route ID; failures return 400 with media_type_mismatch/media_id_mismatch. These conditional guards do not validate every possible JSON property type. The route forwards the body rather than filling missing IDs.

Successful general request POST can auto-enable Spoiler Guard when configured; the separate seasons action does not run that hook.

Quota enrichment preserves upstream unlimited-side representations; missing nextResetAt does not itself mean unlimited.

Collections accepts comma-separated positive movie IDs, one to nine digits. It ignores malformed values and duplicates. Input is limited to 1100 characters and 100 distinct IDs; invalid/oversized input returns 400. Response:

{"results":{"603":{"id":2344,"name":"The Matrix Collection","posterPath":"/poster.jpg","backdropPath":"/backdrop.jpg"},"999":null}}

null means a successful lookup found no collection; failed/refused lookups are omitted. Seerr movie detail is used first; a configured TMDB key enables fallback when Seerr names no collection.

Setup failure returns 503, missing caller claim 403; failed caller linkage after a supplied claim returns 200 {"results":{}}. It is no-store.

TV-by-studio queries TMDB directly and returns a Seerr-shaped discover page. It needs enabled Seerr and a TMDB key, but does not impose the ordinary linked-user prerequisite before querying TMDB.

Only titles accessible in the caller's library receive library/media status enrichment.

It uses studioId, page, supported sortBy values (popularity, first_air_date, vote_average, vote_count, name, original_name, each with .asc or .desc), and the discover filters a series takes, under TMDB discover/tv's names. Unsupported sorts are ignored, and so is a filter value not of its parameter's shape (dates YYYY-MM-DD, numbers, comma- or pipe-separated ids or two-letter languages, two-letter upper-case regions, short ratings).

Setup returns 503, invalid ID/page 400, TMDB failure 502, cancellation 499; parental filtering still applies.

docs.title: Seerr cache behavior
docs.text:
Use these caching rules when deciding whether a response may be stale.

Shared response entries cover content-only genre sliders, genre/keyword lookups, and person resources. Search, discovery, details, similar/recommendation, and collection responses are caller-scoped. Parentally restricted GETs are filtered even on cache hits. Watchlist and issues bypass normal response caching.

Negative user lookup is cached for 60 seconds. Successful request creation evicts corresponding cached movie/TV detail and subresources. Saving plugin configuration clears Seerr caches.

Reachability uses a separate 30-second cache; disabling normal response caching does not imply every status request probes upstream. Expect stale cached metadata until its TTL or invalidation event.

docs.title: TMDB Proxy & Metadata
docs.text:
Use local GUID routes for Jellyfin metadata, the generic TMDB route for external metadata, and Seerr-backed helpers when working through Seerr.

Setting Default What it does TMDB API Key "" TMDB_API_KEY; required by the generic proxy and provider batch. Default Region "US" DEFAULT_REGION; fallback for regional provider lookup. Method Path Access Inputs → response GET studio/{studioId} Authenticated Jellyfin GUID → {id,name,tmdbId,type}. A studio is answered to any caller; another item only when the caller can see it, else 404. GET boxset/{boxsetId} Authenticated Jellyfin BoxSet GUID → {id,name,tmdbId,type}; 404 for a box set the caller cannot see. GET genre/{genreId} Authenticated Jellyfin GUID → {id,name,type}. A genre is answered to any caller; another item only when the caller can see it, else 404. GET person/{personId} Authenticated Jellyfin GUID, optional query itemId GUID → person info. A person is answered to any caller; another item only when the caller can see it, else 404. GET people/info Authenticated Query ids (GUID list), optional itemId → {"people":{"<personIdN>":<info>}}. GET tmdb/search/person Seerr-linked Required nonblank query → Seerr search response, page 1. GET tmdb/search/keyword Seerr-linked Required nonblank query → Seerr keyword-search response. GET tmdb/genres/movie Seerr-linked Upstream Seerr movie genre list. GET tmdb/genres/tv Seerr-linked Upstream Seerr TV genre list. GET tmdb/validate Administrator Supplied query apiKey → {"ok":true}. GET tmdb/{**apiPath} Authenticated TMDB /3/ resource path and query → upstream TMDB JSON/status. GET watch-providers Authenticated Query items, optional region → regional flat-rate provider map. GET jellyseerr/streaming-region Authenticated The caller's Seerr streaming region (own setting, else Seerr's global) → { region, source } (US when Seerr has none set, as Seerr itself does). GET logo/{size}/{file} Anonymous size w45 or w92, file a logo file name the server has seen in a Logos lookup, spelled exactly as TMDB spells it (case-sensitive) → the image from the server's cache; 404 otherwise.

Local lookups return 404 if absent and 500 on lookup errors. Boxset checks type; single studio/genre/person actions do not explicitly enforce their named type. They are local metadata lookups, rather than Seerr proxies.

Batch people ignores malformed/empty GUIDs, de-duplicates, and rejects no valid IDs or more than 100 distinct valid IDs with 400. Missing/non-Person batch entities are omitted.

Person info extends {id,name,tmdbId,type} with nullable birthDate, deathDate, birthPlace, currentAge, ageAtDeath, ageAtItemRelease, and boolean isDeceased.

Optional itemId contributes its premiere date only when accessible to the caller. Optional TMDB enrichment falls back to local data after failure or six seconds. Person reads can return 499 on disconnect.

curl -G -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  --data-urlencode 'ids=9285e8b54149414941494edb9e464dcd' \
  "$JE_URL/people/info"

curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  "$JE_URL/tmdb/movie/603?language=en-US"

The generic proxy uses the saved key, returning 503 if absent. It forwards TMDB paths/query to /3/ using that key.

Restricted callers can receive 403 with code:"parental_block" for unclassified/list/search/discover/trending paths, denied titles, or query parameters outside language, page, region, include_adult, query. Classified title resources are checked against parental policy. The named search/genre helpers above instead use Seerr setup, caller linkage, and proxy errors.

Successful generic responses use Cache-Control: private, no-cache, ETag and 304 revalidation.

Server caching is 30 minutes for query paths such as search/discover/trending, six hours for lookups, and ten minutes for JSON 404 responses. A query string on a title lookup does not itself select the shorter TTL.

Compatible cold movie/TV title, release-date, provider, and review requests can join one bundled upstream lookup; path, query, and cache state determine whether bundling is possible. Other upstream statuses are retained; connection exceptions return 500, disconnect 499.

TMDB validation tests the supplied key, including an unsaved value: blank key 400, rejected key 401, other upstream statuses retained, connection exception 500, with {ok:false,message} failures.

docs.title: Batch watch providers
docs.text:
Look up regional flat-rate providers for multiple movies or TV titles in one request.

items contains comma-separated movie:<id>/tv:<id> keys. IDs must be positive and one to nine digits. Malformed entries are ignored, equivalent numeric IDs de-duplicated. Maximum input length is 2048 characters and maximum distinct valid keys 100; empty/invalid/oversized input returns 400.

Explicit nonempty region must be two uppercase letters. Omitted/empty region uses normalized Default Region, falling back to US if invalid. No Elsewhere UI toggle is required.

curl -G -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  --data-urlencode 'items=movie:603,tv:1399' --data-urlencode 'region=US' \
  "$JE_URL/watch-providers"

{"region":"US","results":{"movie:603":[{"provider_id":8,"provider_name":"Netflix","logo_path":"/logo.jpg"}],"tv:1399":null}}

Provider names/availability in the example are illustrative. Only usable flat-rate entries are retained. [] means no retained provider; null means refused, failed, or unusable lookup. Parentally denied titles get null results.

Missing key/setup returns 503; cancellation 499. Successful responses use private revalidation, ETag and 304.

docs.title: Logo images
docs.text:
The Logos tag group's images come from GET /JellyfinEnhanced/logo/{size}/{file} (for example logo/w92/pbpMk2JmcoNnQwx5JGpXngfoWtp.jpg). The route is anonymous like the CDN assets, because an <img> cannot send a Jellyfin token, but it is not an open TMDB proxy: only the sizes w45 and w92 and PNG, JPEG or WebP file names that came back from the server's own provider or company/network lookups are served. TMDB's image paths are case-sensitive, so a file name must match the lookup's spelling exactly: any other casing is an unknown file and returns 404 before the server's image cache, its failure cache or TMDB is consulted. The server fetches a missing image from TMDB's image server once (at most 256 KiB, image/* only, SVG refused), keeps it under Jellyfin's cache directory in jellyfin-enhanced/logos (at most 64 MB for both sizes together: past that the least recently read images are deleted and fetched again when asked for; a start removes abandoned downloads and files no lookup names), and answers with Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800, a strong ETag and 304 revalidation. A failed fetch returns 404 and is retried after ten minutes. Native Poster Tags draw the same cached files and never fetch during a poster request: a poster built on demand (server cache off, or no entry yet) uses the stored lookups only, draws the name chip or no logo for that render, and queues the missing lookups and images for one background warm (within the same concurrency and rate limits) that later posters pick up.

Privacy

Browsers never contact TMDB for logos: the lookups and image downloads run on the server with the server's TMDB key, and clients only see the names and image paths in the tag cache. Without a key or internet access the group shows names.

docs.title: Spoiler Guard
docs.text:
Use caller routes to manage protection without replacing the raw state file.

All caller actions require a nonempty user-ID claim. Enable actions additionally resolve an existing caller and accessible item; administrator credentials cannot select another user through these URLs. See Spoiler Guard settings for the administrator policy.

Setting Default What it does Enable Spoiler Guard false SpoilerBlurEnabled; gates pending POST and apply-existing preview/start. Other state-management routes remain callable. Auto-enable Spoiler Guard on Seerr request false SpoilerAutoEnableOnSeerrRequest; hooks successful general Seerr request POSTs, alongside the master setting.

docs.title: Spoiler Guard on title responses
docs.text:
The Seerr proxy, the TMDB passthrough's title routes and mdblist-ratings/{mediaType}/{tmdbId} apply the caller's Spoiler Guard policy to protected titles, on top of their shared caches.

Response Effect Seerr and TMDB title details Fields follow the caller's settings. Adds jeSpoilerGuard: true, jeSpoilerGuardInherited: true for a movie protected only through a collection, jeSpoilerGuardItems with the guarded library items, and jeYear when dates are hidden, also on seasons and episodes. Seerr keywords move to jeRuleKeywords, for request override rules. A started season or played episode stays visible when the library holds its TMDB id. A season's own response also accepts its TVDB id. Seerr lists overview becomes the placeholder and ratings are removed, per setting. Dates stay. A removed score moves to jeSortRating and a removed vote count to jeSortVotes, so Top Rated and Most votes keep their order. In a person's combined_credits, a protected title's cast row also loses character when titles or descriptions are hidden, as on its details. Seerr ratings, TMDB movie/{id}/release_dates Empty when ratings or dates are hidden. TMDB title routes no-store, with no ETag, so a stored unprotected copy can't be revalidated. Follow-ups to protected details Ratings, season and TMDB requests can send X-JE-Spoiler-Guarded with the jeSpoilerGuardItems of their details, or 1, because they carry only a TMDB id. It can only hide more. Items that aren't the caller's guards are ignored. mdblist-ratings {Found:false,Confirmed:false} when ratings are hidden. arr/queue, arr/history, arr/calendar Episode titles are removed from subtitles, per caller, on top of the shared caches. arr/requests Dates are removed when hidden. isComingSoon keeps its value.

docs.title: State and preferences
docs.text:
Read your protection lists and preferences here. Preference POSTs replace the complete preference object.

Method Path Access Request → response GET spoiler-blur/series Caller Full {Series,Movies,Collections,PendingTmdb,Prefs} state; no-store. GET spoiler-blur/movies/{movieId}/in-scope Caller {inScope} for the caller's own state: on their Movies list or in an opted-in collection; no-store. Invalid id → 400; a failed collection lookup → 503, so a client can keep its protection. GET spoiler-blur/user-prefs Caller SpoilerBlurUserPrefs object. POST spoiler-blur/user-prefs Caller Complete preference object, at most 8 KiB → {success:true,prefs:<submitted preferences>}.

The four dictionaries default to {} and use case-insensitive keys. Library keys are N-format GUIDs. Pending keys are movie:<tmdbId> or tv:<tmdbId>.

Dictionary Entry fields (strings default to "") Series SeriesId, SeriesName, EnabledAt Movies MovieId, MovieName, EnabledAt Collections CollectionId, CollectionName, EnabledAt PendingTmdb MediaType, TmdbId, DisplayName, RequestedAt

EnabledAt/RequestedAt are ISO timestamps. Collection protection applies to member movies; the collection itself remains the entry point.

Prefs defaults to this object (null fields can be omitted on the wire):

{
  "HideSeriesDescriptions": null,
  "HideEpisodeDescriptions": null,
  "HideTags": null,
  "HideChapterNames": null,
  "HideTaglines": null,
  "HideRatings": null,
  "HideAirDate": null,
  "ReplaceEpisodeTitles": null,
  "HideCast": null,
  "HideReviews": null,
  "HideTrickplay": null,
  "UseAdvancedCategories": null,
  "SkipDisableConfirm": false
}

Nullable category flags inherit policy with null, and opt out of stripping with false. True never enables a category that the administrator disabled. HideTrickplay=false opts out of trickplay seek-preview protection (SpoilerBlurTrickplay). UseAdvancedCategories=false instead restores uniform stripping by opting out of category reveals.

POST replaces preferences rather than patching them; missing body returns 400.

Missing files return default state/preferences with 200. These caller reads strict-read existing files: corrupt data is backed up/reset and reported as 503 {success:false,message} with a corruption event.

Preference write failures return 503 for corruption or 500 for other failures. The raw own/admin spoilerblur.json GET remains lenient.

curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" "$JE_URL/spoiler-blur/series"
curl -X POST "$JE_URL/spoiler-blur/user-prefs" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"HideReviews":false}'

docs.title: Enable, disable, and pending protection
docs.text:
Add or remove protection for library items. Use pending protection for TMDB titles that may be added to your library later.

Method Path Body/query → response POST spoiler-blur/series/{seriesId} No body → {success:true,seriesId,name}. DELETE spoiler-blur/series/{seriesId} No body → {success:true,seriesId,removed}. POST spoiler-blur/movies/{movieId} Optional JSON {MovieName:"…"}, 8 KiB → {success:true,movieId,name}. DELETE spoiler-blur/movies/{movieId} No body → {success:true,movieId,removed}. POST spoiler-blur/collections/{collectionId} Optional JSON {CollectionName:"…"}, 8 KiB → {success:true,collectionId,name}. DELETE spoiler-blur/collections/{collectionId} No body → {success:true,collectionId,removed}. POST spoiler-blur/pending/{mediaType}/{tmdbId} Optional query displayName → {success:true,promoted,jellyfinId,name}. DELETE spoiler-blur/pending/{mediaType}/{tmdbId} No body → {success:true,removed,removedFrom,jellyfinId} when removed.

Library IDs must parse as GUIDs (400 otherwise). POST requires the correct accessible Series/Movie/BoxSet type (404 for missing, inaccessible, or wrong type); unresolved caller returns 403.

Supplied movie/collection names have markup and angle brackets removed and are capped at 200 characters. Re-enabling preserves the existing timestamp. DELETE is idempotent: absent protection returns 200 with removed:false.

Pending type is normalized to movie/tv; TMDB ID must parse as a positive integer (400 otherwise). Optional displayName is capped at 200 characters with control/format characters removed. Master off returns 503.

Existing accessible titles may promote immediately, returning promoted:"series" or "movie" with a Jellyfin ID/name; otherwise promoted:"pending" with null/omitted ID/name. Future library additions can promote pending entries automatically.

New pending entries cap at 500 per user (429, code:"pending_cap_exceeded"); existing entries can still be updated/promoted.

Pending DELETE can remove both pending and promoted protection. A no-op returns {"success":true,"removed":false,"removedFrom":"none"}; successful removal names series, movie, or pending.

These mutations strict-read and return 503 on corruption, 500 on storage errors.

curl -X POST -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  "$JE_URL/spoiler-blur/series/9285e8b54149414941494edb9e464dcd"
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  "$JE_URL/spoiler-blur/pending/tv/1399?displayName=Game%20of%20Thrones"

docs.title: Health and apply-existing task
docs.text:
Use health routes to review and acknowledge recorded corruption events. As an administrator, you can also preview, start, and monitor protection for existing titles in the saved auto-enable scope.

Method Path Access Contract GET spoiler-blur/health Caller/admin {healthy,corruptionEvents:[{userId,userDisplay,at,reason}]}. DELETE spoiler-blur/health/{targetUserId} Own/admin Acknowledge event → {"success":true}. GET spoiler-blur/apply-existing/preview Administrator Optional skipStarted=false → dry-run summary. POST spoiler-blur/apply-existing Administrator Optional skipStarted=false, no body → 202 {success:true,taskId,completedRuns}. GET spoiler-blur/apply-existing/status Administrator {taskId,state,progress,completedRuns,lastRun}; no-store.

Health reports retained process-lifetime corruption history, rather than testing the blur engine. Viewers see self, administrators all users. DELETE accepts a parseable target GUID (400 otherwise); cross-user denial is 403. Acknowledgment clears the event, rather than repairing files.

Preview/start use the saved auto-enable scope and return 409 if the master is off or a run is busy.

Preview failure returns 500; start returns 503 if the scheduled task is unavailable.

Status works independently of the master toggle, returning state:"Unavailable" with null task/progress if no worker exists. Run history/counters are since server start.

Apply-existing summary fields

Summary fields are DryRun, SkipStarted, SeriesInScope, MoviesInScope, Users, UsersAffected, SeriesArmed, MoviesArmed, AlreadyArmed, SkippedWatched, SkippedStarted, UsersFailed, Cancelled, nullable Error, StartedAt, nullable FinishedAt, ElapsedMs, and PerUser.

Each PerUser entry has UserId, UserName, IsDisabled, VisibleTitles, Series, Movies, AlreadyArmed, SkippedWatched, SkippedStarted, Failed. Status lastRun uses this same summary, or null before a completed run.

curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  "$JE_URL/spoiler-blur/apply-existing/preview?skipStarted=true"

docs.title: Tags, Cache & Watch Data
docs.text:
Use these own/admin routes to retrieve data visible to the target account. Missing target accounts or inaccessible items return 404; unauthorized target access 403; invalid typed GUIDs/query values can return 400. Metadata may be stripped by Spoiler Guard.

Setting Default What it does Server-Side Tag Cache true TagCacheServerMode; gates cached delivery and rebuild. Enable Tag Styles false TagStylesEnabled; enables effective overrides. Apply to (Tag Styles) "both" TagStyleTarget; both, web, or native. Preset (Tag Styles) "default" TagStylePreset; default, glass, outline, dark, light, mono or poster. Let users pick their own preset false TagStylesAllowUserPreset; honours each user's TagStylePreset (below). Enable Native Poster Tags (Experimental) false NativePosterTagsEnabled; delivery toggle, rather than a preview prerequisite. Method Path Access Request → response POST tag-cache/rebuild Administrator No body → {success:true,message:"Tag cache rebuild started in the background."}. GET admin/leaving-soon Administrator No body → the Leaving soon source state {Configured, Maintainerr, Actions, HomeRow, Collections, CollectionsFound, Items, Dated, LastSuccess, LastAttempt, NextRefresh, LastError} (times Unix ms or null; LastError a short reason such as HTTP 500, timed out or not reachable; Actions whether the item-menu actions are on; HomeRow one of off, unknown, registered, hss-missing, ft-missing, failed). Never the URL, key or collection names. POST admin/leaving-soon/refresh Administrator No body → reads the Leaving soon source now (Maintainerr and/or the leaving collections), publishes changed Leaving facts to the tag cache, then answers the state as above. GET maintainerr/item/{itemId} Administrator No body → {ItemId, Marked, CollectionId, CollectionName, DeleteAt, Supported} from the last read (no Maintainerr call): whether Maintainerr lists the item, in which of its collections (id and title, when the collections were read), its delete time (Unix ms or null) and whether the actions handle its kind (movies and series). 404 while the actions are off (LeavingSoonMaintainerrActions off or no Maintainerr URL) or the item is unknown. POST maintainerr/mark Administrator {itemId} → the state above after the change. Adds the item to the one active manual Maintainerr collection of its type on its library (POST /api/collections/media/add, action 0); two collections on one library are told apart by asking each one's Radarr/Sonarr server (as Maintainerr lists them, GET /api/settings/radarr|sonarr) whether it holds the item (/api/v3/movie?tmdbId=, /api/v3/series?tvdbId=, same address guard). Then the facts are read again and published, so badges and the home row follow at once. 400 {error} when no collection fits (the reason names Maintainerr's collections), the item is already marked or is not a movie or series; 502 {error} with Maintainerr's reason (or a short one: not reachable, timed out, redirected (redirects are not followed)) when the request failed. Never the address or key. POST maintainerr/unmark Administrator {itemId} → the state after the change. Removes the item from the Maintainerr collection holding it (action 1), then reads again. 400 when it is not marked. POST maintainerr/postpone Administrator {itemId, days?} → the state after the change. days 1–3650 moves the removal that much later (POST /api/collections/media/postpone); without days the timer restarts from today. 400 when the item is not marked or days is out of range. POST admin/configuration Administrator {Changes:{Field:value}, Expected?:{Field:value}} (PluginConfiguration field names, values as GET /Plugins/{id}/Configuration returns them) → {values:{Field:stored}}. Writes only these fields on top of the configuration the server holds now, through the normal configuration save and inside its critical section: a full configuration save that lands while the request waits is kept, never put back, and so is the server's own write of a field in place (maintenance toggle clear, translation refresh signal, analytics state), which takes the same lock. A field in Expected is the value read before editing it: when the server's value differs from it and from the new value, nothing is written and the answer is 409 {conflicts:{Field:serverValue}}. Only the Media Tags tab's own fields are accepted (those its section modules declare, Helpers/MediaTagsPageFields.cs); any other field, API keys included, is 400 naming it, and nothing is written. Each value is checked with the normalisers the server uses for that field (TagLayoutRules, TagShapeRules, LanguageTagDisplay, TagLookValidation, RatingSourceSettings, TagStyleSet, the anchor positions): an unknown, empty or blank layout, density, position, target, preset or source (none of the server's own values has an empty "inherit"), a number outside its range (day windows and cache lifetime 1–365, order 1–99, minimum score 0–10, caps 0–10), a text over its limit (1024 characters unless the field has its own), more than 500 server-wide item looks (TagLookItemOverrides, also refused when an entry would be dropped or merged) or a document the normaliser would drop is 400 {error:"Invalid value for 'Field': reason."}; accepted values are stored in their canonical spelling and returned. The entire body, including Changes, Expected and JSON escaping, is limited to 8 MiB: a larger one is refused while it is read, before anything is checked or written (Jellyfin's exception middleware answers 500 "Error processing request."). Used by the Media Tags admin tab and by the item editor's For everyone (TagLookItemOverrides only, using the per-entry mutation below). GET tag-cache/summary Administrator No body → {enabled, entries, lastModified, rebuilding}: whether the server tag cache is on, how many items it holds, its last change (Unix ms, 0 = never) and whether a full build is running or a manual one is queued. Counts are 0 while the cache is off. Used by the Media Tags admin tab's Overview. GET tag-cache/{userId} Own/admin Optional since signed 64-bit cursor and, with it, known (the filterRevision of the caller's copy) → cache envelope below; ETag/304. POST tag-data/{userId} Own/admin Raw nonempty string array, at most 200 IDs; optional mediaSourceId, optional latestEpisode=true → {Items:[<item>],StripRevision}. Named-source scores missing for a title are fetched from MDBList for at most two seconds before the response; the fetch then finishes in the background, and the response carries the scores cached by then. An item whose scores were still being fetched carries RatingsPending: true (omitted otherwise): treat its rating facts as provisional and ask again soon; the web client re-asks after a minute. RatingsRefreshAt (Unix ms, omitted when no named source is in use or the title has no TMDB id) is when the item's named-source scores stop being current: a minute ahead while they are due, the retry time after a failed lookup (last good scores are kept meanwhile), else seven days after a found answer or three after a confirmed miss. Keep the answer no longer than that. GET status-tags/series?ids=… Authenticated, user-filtered Up to 50 series item IDs → {id:{status,lastAired,nextAired,seasonEpisodes}}; see below. GET status-tags/trending Authenticated {source,movies,series} trending ranks for Status Tags; see below. GET item-stats/{userId}/{itemId} Own/admin Optional mediaSourceId → {success,size,progress,totalPlaybackTicks,totalRuntimeTicks}. GET file-size/{userId}/{itemId} Own/admin Optional mediaSourceId → {success,size}. GET watch-progress/{userId}/{itemId} Own/admin {success,progress,totalPlaybackTicks,totalRuntimeTicks}. GET tag-styles Authenticated Effective web override set. GET tag-styles/catalog Authenticated Shipped labels and palettes only; no administrator configuration. GET native-poster-tags/preview/{itemId} Administrator JPEG diagnostic preview; query below.

Changes.TagLookItemOverrides also accepts {Set:[itemLook,...], Remove:[itemId,...], Expected:{itemId:previousEntryOrNull,...}}. Every affected id must occur once across Set/Remove and in Expected; null means no entry was present. The server checks all affected entries and merges the update into the latest list inside one configuration write lock. A target changed meanwhile causes 409 with the latest list; unrelated changes are kept. The item editor retries once after a fresh read. Editor, Rules-list remove and entry Undo send only affected entries, with at most 500 distinct affected IDs across Set and Remove. The Rules store captures this per-entry intent and its Expected stamps when the user acts, then rebases pending operations onto each save response; newly returned remote entries never become implicit removals. A canceled delta resolves locally without a PATCH only before a write starts or after a definitive rejection (a conflict, or a 4xx body naming the field); other fields in the same atomic patch still save. Network errors, 5xx responses and lost responses leave the write outcome unknown, so pending intent, including Undo, requires a successful acknowledging PATCH before the page reports saved. A validated empty mutation from an older client succeeds without writing configuration. An addition that would exceed the final-list cap of 500 without a corresponding removal is refused.

Portable import and import Undo are explicit whole-list replacements: Changes.TagLookItemOverrides is an array/null and Expected.TagLookItemOverrides is the whole list the page read. They are never converted to per-entry mutations. Replacement is bounded by the final-list cap of 500 and the 8 MiB body envelope, so replacing 500 entries with 500 disjoint entries is supported even though a mutation would affect 1,000 IDs. Edits made before the replacement is acknowledged fold into its pending value; failure preserves the whole replacement for Retry, and Keep mine / Take theirs resolves that entire list. Only after successful acknowledgement do ordinary per-entry edits use the mutation transport again.

The admin import preview and configuration patch both allow 8 MiB including JSON escaping and Expected. A 500-entry list populated with the largest valid looks (nine slots and caps, two fully populated shape looks, 64-character colour preset, maximum timestamp) measures 926,353 bytes in an admin export and 1,846,076 bytes in a replacement with both Changes and Expected, leaving over four times headroom. Single-entry edit/remove/Undo requests measure 1,957–3,798 bytes. User import/preset endpoints retain their 64 KiB limit.

The Tier 2 page allowlist also includes TagScale, TagGap, TagEdgeSpacing; AwardsTagsEnabled, AwardsTagsPosition, AwardsTagsImdb, AwardsTagsCertifiedFresh, AwardsTagsOscar, AwardsTagsEmmy, AwardsTagsLetterboxd, AwardsTagsImdbList, AwardsTagsLetterboxdList, AwardsTagsRefreshHours; LogoTagsEnabled, LogoTagsPosition, LogoTagsMovieMode, LogoTagsSeriesMode, LogoTagsRegion, LogoTagsMaxLogos; and CustomTagsEnabled, CustomTagsPosition, CustomTagRules. The list fields require a numeric id or owner/slug, cadence is 1–168 hours, logo maximum is 1–2, and an empty logo region follows the server. Custom documents must contain at most 20 complete distinct rules accepted by CustomTagRuleSet (valid match, bounded value and label, non-reserved label and known optional icon). Invalid patches are refused as a whole. CustomTagRuleKey and CustomTagRuleSources are never page fields and return 400. The legacy Tag Styles preset alias custom is accepted as default; blank presets are refused.

The Tier 3 Leaving soon section adds StatusTagsLeaving and StatusTagsDirectPlay. The Maintainerr source belongs to the Services tab's form, not to this patch: LeavingSoonMaintainerrUrl (empty, or an http(s) address without credentials, query or fragment; 512 characters), LeavingSoonMaintainerrApiKey (printable ASCII without spaces; 256 characters), LeavingSoonCollections (at most 20 names of at most 200 characters, one per line or comma separated; 4096 characters), LeavingSoonRefreshHours (1–168), LeavingSoonMaintainerrActions and LeavingSoonHomeRow (switches, both on by default; each only acts with a Maintainerr URL) are saved with the configuration page (LeavingSoonService.NormalizeSource checks them on every full save: a value its contract refuses keeps the stored one and is logged by name), and this patch answers 400 naming any of them.

curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" "$JE_URL/tag-cache/$USER_ID"
curl -X POST "$JE_URL/tag-data/$USER_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '["9285e8b54149414941494edb9e464dcd"]'
curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  "$JE_URL/item-stats/$USER_ID/9285e8b54149414941494edb9e464dcd"

docs.title: Tag cache and batch shape
docs.text:
Use the cache for full snapshots or updates since a cursor. Use tag-data to fetch a batch of items directly, including when cached delivery is disabled. Web cards look up their valid data-id/data-itemid before the artwork URL, so an episode borrowing its season's poster requests the episode's data. Without a valid card id, the artwork id remains a fallback.

Cache disabled returns 404 for GET and 400 for rebuild. A busy rebuild returns 409. Cached response:

{"version":1,"timestamp":1767441600000,"servedAt":1767441601000,"filterRevision":"EXAMPLE","filterBase":"EXAMPLEBASE","count":0,"items":{},"reviewRatings":{}}

A delta (?since=1767441600000) that removes two items:

{"version":1,"timestamp":1767441700000,"servedAt":1767441701000,"filterRevision":"EXAMPLE","filterBase":"EXAMPLEBASE","removed":["0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9","9f8e7d6c5b4a39281706f5e4d3c2b1a0"],"count":0,"items":{}}

items maps Jellyfin item IDs to TagCacheEntry objects. timestamp, servedAt, and entry LastUpdated use Unix milliseconds; version identifies a cache generation. The version changes only with a full rebuild swap, a server-mode transition, or when more than 20,000 removals have accumulated since the last swap. Every other change (library updates, MDBList ratings, logos, scenes, awards, Leaving soon, Custom tag re-matches, series inheritance, air-date boundaries) raises the changed entries' LastUpdated and reaches clients through ?since= as a delta, so a browser downloads only those entries. A removed item (deleted, moved into an excluded library, or swept by a reconcile) reaches a delta as its id in removed, an array present only when the delta removes something: delete those ids from your copy. An id that came back after its removal arrives in items instead, never in both. Removal stamps follow the same clock as LastUpdated and are kept with the on-disk snapshot, so a removal made before a server restart still reaches a client whose cursor predates it. removed lists ids only and is not filtered by access: a removed item has no facts left to protect. LastUpdated stamps strictly increase: each is the server's millisecond clock, or one past the newest stamp already issued, so two updates in the same millisecond never share a stamp and ?since=<cursor> (which returns entries with LastUpdated greater than the cursor) cannot skip the later one.

A full snapshot can be read in pages: ?limit=2000 (100 to 5,000) returns the first entries in ordinal id order with next, the last id of the page, while more follow; ask again with &after=<next> until a page has no next. Every page carries the generation's version, filterRevision and filterBase; if a page's version or filterRevision differs from the first page's, start over. Then fetch one delta since the first page's timestamp: it carries every entry changed and every id removed while you paged. Under Spoiler Guard, pages are stripped like a full response and carry the same filterRevision. Without limit, the whole snapshot comes in one response, as before. The server answers each page from one ordinally sorted key index shared by every page and every caller, rebuilt only when an entry is added or removed (or the snapshot is replaced), so a page costs a binary search plus the entries it returns, not a sort of the remaining keys; next is always a key the caller can see.

Use the returned timestamp as the next since cursor, rather than an ISO timestamp or servedAt. Deltas include changed entries plus guarded entries so watched/protection changes update their metadata. servedAt orders stored snapshots across restarts.

If filterRevision changes, your copy may hold entries the user can no longer see, or entries stripped under another Spoiler Guard policy, which a delta cannot correct. filterBase is the same fingerprint without the access part. Send the revision your copy was made under as known with a delta (?since=…&known=EXAMPLE): when it differs from the current one, the response also carries visible, every item ID the user can see now (sorted; it never names an item they cannot see). Its items then also include, freshly projected for the user's current access, every visible entry whose content depends on access whatever its LastUpdated: series and seasons whose quality, languages, latest episode or status facts come from episodes, and entries with a collection-made Custom Tag or Leaving fact. If filterBase is unchanged and your copy holds every visible ID (after applying the delta's items), only access changed: delete the entries not in visible, apply the delta, and keep the copy under the new filterRevision. Otherwise (Spoiler Guard or rating-source change, a newly visible item your copy lacks, or no known) fetch a full response and replace your copy. A restricted user's revision changes when an item they cannot see is added, so this keeps such additions to one delta with an ID list rather than a full download. Successful responses support ETag revalidation with Cache-Control: no-cache.

The plugin does not compress responses itself: Jellyfin's response compression encodes JSON with Brotli or gzip whenever the request's Accept-Encoding allows it (Content-Encoding: br, Vary: Accept-Encoding). Browsers always send it; send Accept-Encoding: br, gzip from scripts. A reverse proxy must pass the header through and must not strip the encoding. Measured on a 3,882-entry library (85 series, 231 seasons, 3,447 episodes, 119 movies): a full response is 14.7 MB of JSON and 1.39 MB with Brotli (1.33 MB with gzip), about 360 bytes per entry on the wire.

reviewRatings maps mediaType:tmdbKey to {average,count} under the caller's review visibility rules. It is present only when both Enable User Written Reviews and Show average user rating on poster cards are enabled; otherwise it is null/omitted.

It contains the full aggregate map even on deltas; absent keys mean no visible rated reviews.

Cache entry field Type Type, TmdbId, SeriesTmdbId, OfficialRating, SeriesId, LibraryId Nullable strings SeasonNumber, EpisodeNumber Nullable integers Genres, AudioLanguages, PartialAudioLanguages, SubtitleLanguages Nullable string arrays CommunityRating, CriticRating Nullable numbers Awards Optional immutable title facts: nullable ImdbRank, LetterboxdRank (1–250), booleans CertifiedFresh, OscarWinner, EmmyWinner, nullable OscarYear, EmmyYear; movie/series only, stripped with scores Ratings Optional object of nullable native-unit scores: imdb, tmdb, rtCritic, rtAudience, metacritic, letterboxd, trakt; no key or upstream data means absent LastUpdated Integer milliseconds DateCreated, PremiereDate, LatestEpisodeAdded Nullable integer milliseconds Status Nullable Jellyfin series status string LatestEpisodeAired Nullable integer milliseconds, series/season LatestEpisodeIndex, EpisodeIndex Nullable {Season,Episode,EpisodeEnd,IsLast}; EpisodeEnd is the last episode a combined file covers (S01E09-E10 gives 10) and is omitted for one episode; IsLast is nullable when unresolved and true when the file holds the season's last episode SeasonPremiere Nullable {Season,Aired}; newest regular season's episode 1 for a series, the season's own episode 1 for a season SeasonAddedSpan Nullable {First,Last,Count,CoveredThrough} for season episode added dates; CoveredThrough is the highest N with every episode 1..N in the library (null when not read) StreamData Nullable {Streams,Sources,ItemName,ItemPath} Source, Edition Nullable canonical naming labels, computed server-side before basename trimming CustomTags Nullable string array: the Custom tag rules the item matches (see below) Logos Optional array (at most two) of {kind,name,logo}: kind is provider, network or studio, logo an optional TMDB image path for the logo route below; seasons and episodes carry their series'. Present only while the administrator or at least one user has the Logos group on; removed with the genres by Spoiler Guard's tag strip

The Logos group's per-user settings are LogoTagsEnabled (default false) and LogoTagsPosition (default "bottom-left"), with logos as a group id in TagLayouts, TagGroupOrder and TagGroupCaps (cap 0 shows every logo an entry carries). The administrator's LogoTagsMovieMode (provider, studio, off; default provider), LogoTagsSeriesMode (network, provider, off; default network), LogoTagsRegion (two letters, empty uses DEFAULT_REGION) and LogoTagsMaxLogos (1 or 2, default 1) decide what entries carry; unknown values fall back to the defaults on save. Provider mode falls back to the studio or network when no subscription service is known for the region. Providers come from TMDB watch providers, and network or studio logos from TMDB details matched by name to Jellyfin's studios; both lookups are kept by the server for a day (failures retried after an hour) in tag-logos.json beside the tag cache (a lookup both not refreshed for 31 days and not read by an entry build, batch lookup or native poster for 30 days, such as a title no longer in the library or another region's, is dropped with the logo images only it named; one still read keeps its last data while refreshes fail, for example without a TMDB key), warmed before full builds and the daily reconcile, for batch items within a three-second budget, and in the background for native posters built on demand. Without a TMDB key or internet access entries carry names only.

Source rating preferences are RatingTagsSources (ordered string array; null preserves legacy include switches, empty hides source scores), RatingTagsMinScore (finite 0–10, default 0), and RatingTagsColorByScore (boolean, default false). They are per-user preferences with public admin defaults, seeded for new users and copied by reset-all-users. Unknown source ids and duplicates are removed on save. Ratings is immutable shared metadata, removed with Community/Critic scores by Spoiler Guard.

SubtitleLanguages is the lowercase union of the languages of ordinary (not forced) subtitle tracks, one entry however many SDH tracks share it; a language with only forced tracks is not listed. Series and seasons union their episodes; collections union their members. It follows the same access filtering and Spoiler Guard tag stripping as AudioLanguages; clients must replace their stored cache when filterRevision changes. Ordinary subtitle streams are kept in StreamData.Streams with their hearing-impaired flag and title (for SDH); forced subtitle streams are left out.

CustomTags lists the ids of the administrator's Custom tag rules the item matches, in the rule order of when it was matched. Treat it as a set: the web and native renderers draw matches in the current order of the public CustomTagRules, so reordering rules needs no re-match. A rule id is its match type and 16 hex digits of an HMAC of the match type and lower-cased value under a server-side key (tag:1a2b3c4d5e6f7081, collection:9f2c1e0b7a6d5c4e), so it never names, or lets a client confirm a guess of, the tag or collection. Tags are the item's own plus, for seasons and episodes, their series'; collections are those holding the item or its series, read from one pass over the collections a rule names. A collection match is served only to users whose access set includes a collection that produced it (library access and parental controls, as for the entries themselves); the rule collections a user cannot access are part of the response's filterRevision, so a stored copy is replaced when that access changes. Tag matches are not filtered: the tags are on the item. Clients look rules up by id in the public CustomTagRules and skip unknown ids, so label, icon and colour edits need no cache change. A configuration save that changes the set of matching rules re-matches every entry in the background (metadata only, no media reads; the snapshot stores the rules it was matched under). Collection changes seen by the library monitor patch the affected items, their seasons and episodes. Spoiler Guard's tag strip (SpoilerStripTags, the user's Hide Tags choice) removes it from guarded entries with Genres, in tag-cache, the tag-data stubs and native posters.

LibraryId is the library (collection folder) holding the item in N format; seasons and episodes carry their series'. Entries use the current cache schema (see below); older snapshots are discarded and rebuilt. DateCreated is when the item was added to the library. PremiereDate is set for movies, series and episodes. LatestEpisodeAdded is set for series and seasons (the newest DateCreated among their non-virtual episodes) and for collections (the newest DateCreated among their members of a tagged type, which drives a collection's Just Added badge instead of its own date). It is omitted for a caller who cannot see the episode or member it came from. Null fields are omitted.

StreamData.Streams contains Type, SourceId, Language, Codec, CodecTag, Profile, Height, Width, Channels, ChannelLayout, VideoRangeType, VideoRange (only when the range type is unknown), DisplayTitle; strings/numeric fields can be null. When Spoiler Guard replaces titles or strips overviews for the item, stream titles, ItemName, paths, source names and the naming facts (Source, Edition) are removed, Revision stays, and an audio stream whose title named a commentary or audio-description track carries Role: "secondary", so the main audio is chosen exactly as from the full titles. Sources contains {Id,Path,Name,Source,Edition,RunTimeTicks,Is3D,Revision} (Revision: 12 hex characters hashing Jellyfin's metadata for the version and its streams, covering every input a device profile condition, codec or container check can read, such as anamorphic, reference frames, rotation and Dolby Vision facts; it changes when a replaced or re-encoded file is probed again, not for display-only fields such as stream titles) (Is3D true when Jellyfin reports a 3D format for the version, else omitted); distinct track facts retain SourceId too. The browser remembers the selected merged version and filters streams, All-mode facts and source metadata together; otherwise web and native posters use the first version that has stream facts, else the first listed. These are trimmed tag data, rather than complete Jellyfin item DTOs. Directory paths are never returned; Path and ItemPath are basenames, including for Windows paths on a Unix server. The current persisted entry schema includes Source and Edition; older snapshots are discarded and rebuilt.

Batch tag-data ignores malformed/inaccessible IDs. Items contain Id, Type, Genres, CommunityRating, CriticRating, Ratings, Awards, Logos, CustomTags (collection matches filtered per caller; cache-off matches tags only), OfficialRating, LibraryId, SeriesId, ProviderIds, Name, basename-only Path, nullable Source and Edition, SubtitleLanguages (the selected media sources), trimmed MediaStreams, MediaSources, nullable FirstEpisode, and the nullable Unix-millisecond dates DateCreated, PremiereDate (movies, series and episodes) and LatestEpisodeAdded (series, seasons and collections, only with latestEpisode=true; it counts only episodes, or a collection's members, the target user can see and costs one query per container).

With latestEpisode=true, batch items also carry the applicable Status, LatestEpisodeAired, LatestEpisodeIndex, SeasonPremiere, SeasonAddedSpan and EpisodeIndex facts. Episode sibling lookups use the target user too. The shared cache conservatively omits episode-derived aggregates if any contributor is inaccessible; its server-only StatusEpisodeIds/LatestEpisodeId are excluded from serialization. A changed filterRevision requires replacing stored data. Schema 52 invalidates older disk and IndexedDB copies, including sibling snapshots without the combined distinct quality sets, full All-mode series/season summaries, technical stream and SDH subtitle facts, Scenes, Leaving (including server-only collection provenance), cropped-video widths, version-scoped stream/quality/source facts, audio codec facts from the earlier AC-3/DTS-HD detector, summaries without parallel version-0 audio facts, per-track quality facts from the earlier text-based dynamic range, codec and sound detector, and language and naming facts that counted commentary/description audio, forced-only subtitles and edition or low-quality source words inside titles, per-track sound facts that bucketed channel layouts into 7.1/5.1/2.0, stored subtitle streams that included forced tracks, Atmos facts without their carrier, sound facts that read a bare DTS-HD as Master Audio, missed E-AC-3 JOC Atmos or dropped height channels (5.1.2), language and sound facts that missed commentary named in other scripts, editions without the Redux/Ultimate/Collector's/Anniversary/Uncensored/Open Matte vocabulary, naming facts that read the words of an original-language title under localised metadata as release words, video streams without Jellyfin's coarse VideoRange (stored only when the range type is unknown), facts from the earlier resolution buckets, aspect labels, XviD/DivX codec-tag reading and DTS-HD Master Audio spellings, season and episode scores that took the series' scores over a score of their own, series summaries whose latest-episode extras carried a version count, series/season premiere facts that waited for the UTC instant, and season added spans without episode coverage (SeasonAddedSpan.CoveredThrough, the highest N with every episode 1..N in the library), sound facts that let a track title contradict its stream codec or claim more channels than the track reports, Atmos carriers read from a title before the stream codec, season facts built without multi-episode ranges (a combined file's last episode, and its coverage in full builds), versions without Jellyfin's disc-structure source or 3D format (Sources[].Is3D), version-0 sound facts whose codec and channels came from different tracks or read XLL as DTS:X, and naming facts from the earlier source and edition vocabulary (bare WEB, BR-DISK, HD-DVD, PDTV/Raw-HD, Rogue Cut, Black and Chrome, Masters of Cinema), DOVIInvalid ranges, episode naming facts that read words of the episode's own title as release words, edition facts missed after a title-only file name (Film.Extended.mkv), IMAX facts read from audio or subtitle titles, structured channel layouts that contradicted the track's channel count, DTS streams reported under ffmpeg's dca codec name, episode indexes without a combined file's last episode (EpisodeIndex.EpisodeEnd), sources that let a bare WEB word outrank another source word, Dolby Vision titles whose named base layer was dropped, language facts that counted mul, mis or qaa–qtz as languages, series/season summaries that dropped an alternate version's video facts when the first version was unprobed, resolution facts that measured portrait frames by height, and naming facts that read daily, 1x05 or absolute episode titles as editions, let a trailing release group (-TS) name the source, or lacked BD, DVD5/DVD9, SDTV/TVRip, VHSRip, Hybrid, Producer's/Alternate/Assembly/International Cut and Restored, and naming facts that let a trailing release group stand as the only source (H264-CAM), read a known episode title after a 1x05, daily or absolute marker as release words, treated - 1982 - as an absolute episode number, or ignored .strm names, and resolution facts that read 2560×1600 as 4K, plus summaries whose Latest value came from an unprobed newest episode, naming facts that dropped an edition after a known episode title, read a URL's query string as part of the name, or lacked a remote version's wrapper name, and HDRip/R5/WORKPRINT/PPV, series/season summaries without a summarised source (Categories.source), and version paths that kept a remote address's query string, source summaries ranked by presentation order or by each episode's first version only, interlaced 1080 recorded as 1080p, title-only Dolby Vision SDR without its base, 3D read from 3d/mvc substrings or a release group, explicit edition labels shortened to a known edition, and HDTC, plus versions without a media Revision, interlaced SD (576i/480i) recorded as progressive, and genre-less seasons with a score of their own that did not take their series' genres, and version revisions that left out anamorphic, reference-frame, packet-length, AVC, rotation, Dolby Vision, colour, protocol, timestamp and default-audio facts, sound facts that let a track title's DTS-HD MA/HRA claim contradict the profile the stream reports, video codec facts that missed H.264, VC-1 or MPEG-2 spelled with a dot or hyphen in a title, and naming facts without the Roadshow, Despecialized and Fan Edit editions.

StripRevision is the server-issued revision of all effective data-affecting Spoiler Guard flags: tag stripping, rating stripping and title/overview stream sanitization, including user opt-outs and sorted guarded series/movie/collection sets. none means no relevant strip applies; g2: introduces the broader revision semantics. Bootstrap Prefetched.TagStripRevision comes from the same policy builder. tag-pipeline.js owns this authority, resets it to unknown immediately on user/guard/policy changes and passes each accepted answer's own value as extras.stripRevision. Session and generation checks reject obsolete answers. An invalidation also releases the retired queue drain immediately, so a pending first-episode lookup cannot block fresh guard data; that retired lookup cannot render or stamp its eventual answer.

js/core/tag-renderer-base.js validates every group's hot and persistent fallback entry through one versioned envelope with that revision, payload and timestamp. Unknown authority is a miss without initially deleting stored data; legacy, malformed, expired or mismatched entries are discarded from both tiers. Only authoritative batch answers can write stamped entries; IndexedDB, shared-cache and /Items projections cannot supply authority. Under none, entries may persist across loads; under a guard they are page-only because played state and collection membership may change without changing the policy digest. Empty stripped answers replace old facts and remain hits. Custom's rule fingerprint stays inside its payload. Full/delta refreshes invalidate all or affected fallback entries. Shared-cache access/filterRevision and native collection filtering remain independent requirements.

Streams use the trimmed stream fields listed above, and sources contain basename-only Path and Name.

Container FirstEpisode has {Id,Type,Genres,NeedsStreamFetch:true}; fetch that episode through tag-data for its streams and naming labels. A playable item chooses its naming labels from the highest-resolution version, then source quality for ties. mediaSourceId limits this choice to the requested version. Explicit edition markers precede known words; file and immediate parent-folder names are examined, and .disc stubs take precedence for source. Source/edition labels are removed with the corresponding Spoiler Guard title/tag stripping.

CustomTagRules (plugin configuration, administrators) is an array of at most 20 {Match,Value,Label,Icon} rules: Match is tag or collection, Value the tag or collection name (matched exactly, ignoring case and repeated spaces), Label the chip text and its Tag Styles label (at most 24 characters), Icon null or a genre icon name (theaters, auto_awesome, menu_book, …, the outlined Material Symbols subset JE ships). Saving drops rules with an unknown match type, an empty value or label, or a label of punctuation only (such as *, the Tag Styles whole-group key; every Unicode scalar value is in general category P or is white space, so a supplementary-plane mark such as U+10100 counts, while symbols such as + or $ do not; the configuration page applies the same test), trims and collapses whitespace, cuts labels to 24 characters, drops unknown icons and keeps the first of rules with the same match type and value. CustomTagRuleKey is the secret the rule ids are derived from: generated when rules are first saved, kept across saves (a posted key never replaces a stored one) and never served outside the plugin configuration. The public configuration's CustomTagRules carries only {Id,Label,Icon} per rule, in table order; administrators also get CustomTagRuleSources ({Id,Match,Value}) in the private configuration, which the web client uses for the chip tooltip's source line. CustomTagsEnabled (false) and CustomTagsPosition (top-left) are per-user settings with public admin defaults, like the other groups; the layout settings accept the group id custom (order, caps with default 3, slots).

{"CustomTagRules":[{"Match":"tag","Value":"4K Remaster","Label":"Remaster","Icon":"auto_awesome"},{"Match":"collection","Value":"Criterion","Label":"Criterion","Icon":null}]}

{"CustomTagRules":[{"Id":"tag:1a2b3c4d5e6f7081","Label":"Remaster","Icon":"auto_awesome"},{"Id":"collection:9f2c1e0b7a6d5c4e","Label":"Criterion","Icon":null}]}

The per-user settings document and public admin defaults also carry LanguageTagsShowAudio (true), LanguageTagsShowSubtitles (false), LanguageTagsStyle (flags or codes, default flags) and LanguageTagsCountBadge (off, only, both, default off). Save normalizes unknown styles and modes to their defaults. These change presentation, not the cache facts.

Personal settings.json additionally accepts LanguageTagsPriority (nullable string array) and LanguageTagsPriorityStrict (nullable boolean). The existing own/admin POST user-settings/{userId}/settings.json validates the whole priority list before any write: at most 12 posted entries, each an assigned base ISO 639-1/639-2 code. Names, regional/BCP-47 tags, unknown codes, null entries and und/mul return 400; the previous document stays intact. Codes are trimmed, lowercased and deduplicated in first-occurrence order through the existing audio-language equivalences (eng/en, fre/fra/fr, Tagalog/Filipino, Norwegian variants).

null/missing list means the live administrator LanguageTagsPriority string; [] explicitly disables prioritization. A nonempty personal list replaces that string. Strict null/missing inherits the live administrator boolean independently; true filters and false retains nonprioritized languages. Empty lists never filter. New-user seeding and reset-all leave both fields null. Admin public configuration retains its string/boolean types; personal settings use the array/nullable boolean types above.

The web client serializes saves of each user settings document. It applies a priority edit at its queue turn and restores it on failure before building the next queued document, preserving unrelated edits. Priority controls ignore further edits while saving; after failure, retry from the restored policy.

For example, merge these properties into the complete user document before posting:

{"LanguageTagsPriority":["ja","en","fr"],"LanguageTagsPriorityStrict":null}

Personal matching uses canonical base languages across all codes represented by a grouped flag, with the server's regional merging unchanged. The same policy runs before audio/subtitle chip caps and Dual/Multi counting in web, hub preview and native resolution. Effective terms, strict mode and personal canonical-matching mode participate in the native settings digest and signed image variants; settings saves invalidate the user's native snapshot. No tag-cache entry/schema or access filterRevision change is needed: cached languages remain policy-independent facts. Refresh other open clients to load a saved preference.

Spoiler Guard can strip metadata before return and add Tags on stripped stubs. Series and movie stubs have no ProviderIds but keep the item's TmdbId, so Status Tags can still show a trending rank. mediaSourceId selects a media version; this route does not require cached delivery enabled.

Statistics aggregate playable descendants where applicable. size is bytes, progress an integer percentage, durations Jellyfin ticks (10,000,000 ticks per second). mediaSourceId filters size, rather than watch progress.

docs.title: Status Tags trending list
docs.text:
status-tags/trending returns the server-wide trending ranks behind the Status Tags badges:

{"source":"tmdb-day","movies":{"1084244":54},"series":{"2190":23}}

movies and series map TMDB IDs to 1-based ranks across one combined list of at most 60 movies and series. source is tmdb-day (TMDB trending/all/day, pages 1–3, used when a TMDB API key is configured), seerr-week (Seerr discover/trending, TMDB's weekly list, used without a key or when TMDB does not answer or returns no movies or series), or null with empty maps when neither source answers. Seerr is called with the server API key only, without per-user parental filtering; the list holds only public TMDB IDs and ranks.

Any signed-in user may call it, non-administrators included. The server shares one copy for 30 minutes (5 minutes after an empty answer); saving the plugin configuration drops it. The web client fetches it when Status Tags first render and again after 30 minutes, or after 5 minutes following an empty or failed answer. With Enable Status Tags or Show Trending rank off in the plugin configuration, it returns source:null with empty maps without calling upstream.

docs.title: Status Tags series schedules
docs.text:
GET /JellyfinEnhanced/status-tags/series?ids=<id>,<id> requires authentication and 1–50 comma-separated Jellyfin item-ID strings. An empty request or more than 50 IDs returns 400. Malformed/empty GUIDs, inaccessible items, non-series and series without a positive numeric TMDB ID are omitted. Lookup uses the caller's Jellyfin access (including parental limits and blocked tags); no target-user parameter is accepted.

{"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa":{"status":"Returning Series","lastAired":{"date":"2026-10-28","season":2,"episode":10,"type":"finale"},"nextAired":{"date":"2027-03-01","season":3,"episode":1},"seasonEpisodes":{"1":8,"2":10,"3":8}}}

Item-ID keys use lowercase N-format GUIDs. Missing status/episode facts may be null; air dates are yyyy-MM-dd calendar dates, interpreted in the user's local calendar by the client. type is TMDB's episode_type, read from the latest aired season when absent from tv/{id}. seasonEpisodes is TMDB's episode count per regular season (season number → count; null when TMDB lists none); Complete Season needs it on web and native posters.

The endpoint returns {} without upstream calls while admin StatusTagsEnabled is off or no TMDB key is configured. Authoritative missing upstream series are omitted. Transient upstream failures (including 429, 5xx and transport exceptions) return { "<itemId>": { "retry": true } } for the affected ID. The client retains its prior facts and retries after five minutes while a current card remains visible. Responses containing retry markers use Cache-Control: private, no-store; other responses use Cache-Control: private, max-age=600. TMDB responses are shared in TmdbResponseCache for six hours; credential changes use a separate cache key. At most four upstream lookups run concurrently, with 35 starts per ten-second window. The web client requests visible series and parent series of visible season/episode cards in batches of 50, caches answers for one hour, retries failures after five minutes, and drops stale card/user answers.

docs.title: Leaving soon and direct-play status badges
docs.text:
LeavingSoonService reads the administrator's source on the server only: GET {LeavingSoonMaintainerrUrl}/api/collections (header X-Api-Key when LeavingSoonMaintainerrApiKey is set, 30-second timeout, answers up to 16 MiB, the same address guard as the *arr URLs, through the named client JellyfinEnhanced.Maintainerr, which never follows a redirect: a 3xx answer is a failed refresh that keeps the previous answer, logged once per destination host, so the key never reaches another origin or an unchecked address) and/or the existing collections named in LeavingSoonCollections. A Maintainerr member's delete time is addDate + deleteAfterDays days (Unix ms UTC), and an answer with one more than ten years from now is refused as a failure (a delete date is out of range) that keeps the previous answer; renderers read a stored time no date type can hold as undated; inactive collections are skipped, and a member without a date (or the collection fallback) leaves undated. An empty list, or only inactive or empty collections, is a real empty answer; entries that are not collections and members without a usable id are skipped, but an answer with entries and no collection, or with members and none usable, is a failure that keeps the previous answer. Members match by mediaServerId (a Jellyfin item id) or, for a Plex-backed Maintainerr's movies and shows, by TMDB id. The answer is kept in leaving-soon.json next to the plugin configuration with a digest of the source, never the URL or key. Refresh Leaving Soon Tags (JellyfinEnhancedRefreshLeavingSoonTags) runs hourly and only acts once LeavingSoonRefreshHours (default 6) has passed; a failed request keeps the previous answer and retries after 15 minutes, doubling up to the interval; a source change refreshes at once in the background, and POST admin/leaving-soon/refresh forces one. Changed facts are published as Leaving ({DeleteAt}, Unix ms or null) on the cache entries of the items, their seasons and episodes (the earliest of the item's, its season's and its series'), through the normal generation/cursor boundary (the snapshot records which answer the cache last received, so an answer saved but not published, because the publish was cancelled or the server stopped, is published by the next run even when nothing is due or the answer is unchanged; the tag cache saves a publish on its normal debounce, so every cache load from disk re-applies the snapshot and an older cache file left by a crash or a failed save never shows facts the snapshot has replaced); /tag-data items carry the same Leaving, and served entries drop it while no source is set. A fact that only the leaving collections produced keeps those collections' ids on the server entry and is served (in tag-cache, tag-data and native posters) only to users whose access set includes one of them, like collection-matched CustomTags; the leaving collections a user cannot access are part of the response's filterRevision, and the ids themselves never reach clients. Maintainerr's facts name no Jellyfin collection, so they are served to anyone who can see the item. Card reads never contact Maintainerr. Public configuration has StatusTagsLeaving, StatusTagsDirectPlay (the starting family switches) and LeavingSoonAvailable (whether a source is set), never the source itself.

The direct-play warning is computed in the browser (js/tags/tag-direct-play.js) with Jellyfin's POST /Items/{id}/PlaybackInfo (UserId, the DeviceProfile jellyfin-web 12.1 would send: its browserDeviceProfile ported, because the bundle exposes no handle and the session capabilities the web client registers (/Sessions) carry no profile, with the app host's options for a video and its width/codec settings, or window.NativeShell.AppHost.getDeviceProfile(builder) in an app shell; MaxStreamingBitrate from the user's saved quality for the network, maxbitrate-Video-{IsInNetwork}, or the profile ceiling while automatic detection has measured nothing; tests/fixtures/direct-play-web-12.1-chromium.json holds the real client's profile captured in Chromium, EnableDirectPlay/EnableDirectStream/EnableTranscoding, AutoOpenLiveStream:false, IsPlayback:false; the profile is built again, with a new hash, when the signed-in user or any local setting its build read changes, compared at most once per task; a native shell's late answer applies only while its build's generation is current, which a user change or a changed setting ends at once, and the user and setting values that build read still hold, otherwise it is ignored and the profile built again); items Jellyfin's PlaybackInfo would refresh with a remote probe are not looked up (it does so when the item's path ends in .strm, probed before or not, and when a video's first media source lists no video stream): a .strm file name in the cache entry's StreamData.ItemPath or a StreamData.Sources[].Path (the /tag-data item's Path or MediaSources[].Path), or a stream list whose first source (matched by SourceId when streams carry one) has no Video stream; items with no stream list are looked up. An item with several versions is asked about the one the user picked on its details page (MediaSourceId in the query and body, when it is one of the item's versions), and answers are kept per item and version; the media source with that id, else the first media source, has its SupportsDirectPlay, SupportsDirectStream and TranscodeReasons (or the TranscodeReasons query of its TranscodingUrl) decide the badge. Requests are sent with fetch and the headers ApiClient sends (ApiClient.ajax takes no abort signal and sets no timeout on a POST): its own Authorization from setRequestHeaders, MediaBrowser Client="…", Device="…", DeviceId="…", Version="…", Token="…" (composed from its accessors where it has no such method), so the server attributes each lookup to this browser's session and device, each with a 15-second deadline covering the answer's body: past it the request is aborted, its slot frees at once, an answer arriving later is ignored, and the item counts as a failed lookup (asked again after ten minutes). At most two requests are on the network at once; a reset (renderer teardown, user switch) drops their answers but not their slots, which free when they settle or reach their deadline. Answers are stored in the browser's tag cache store (IndexedDB database version 3, store directPlay, keyed scope|profileHash|itemId, the hash covering the profile and the bitrate, at most 2,000 per scope) for a day. No plugin endpoint is involved and native posters never draw it.

docs.title: Style and native-preview contracts
docs.text:
Read effective web styles or the shipped style catalog. As an administrator, use native preview to inspect how tags render on an item's artwork.

tag-styles (any signed-in user) returns every chip's effective colours, already resolved field by field (label override, then group override, then the preset palette). Optional preset query: the caller's own preset, honoured only while Let users pick their own preset is on; otherwise the admin's preset applies.

{"v":2,"preset":"glass",
 "quality":{"*":{"background":"rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.161)","border":"rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.349)","color":"rgba(255, 255, 255, 1)"},"4K":{…}},
 "age":[{"ratings":["PG-13","TV-14"],"background":"…","border":"…","color":"…"}],
 "ageDefault":{…},
 "rating":{"community":{…},"critic":{…},"userReview":{…}},
 "genre":{"*":{…},"horror":{…},"science fiction":{…}},
 "status":{"added":{…},"newMovie":{…},"newSeries":{…},"newEpisode":{…},"trending":{…}},
 "language":{"background":null,"border":"…","color":null},
 "logos":{"provider":{…},"company":{…},"text":{…}},
 "custom":{"*":{…},"Remaster":{…}}}

Colour objects have background, border, color (null keeps the built-in colour). quality and the status/rating maps list only chips with a non-default colour; * covers quality labels outside the catalog and ageDefault age ratings outside the colour sheet. age lists each age board with every rating it covers. custom has * (every Custom chip) and each Custom label with a colour of its own; genre likewise has * (every genre chip: the preset and group colours) and each genre label with a colour of its own, which the web matches on the chip's data-je-genre (only these entries colour the genre's .genre-text name too; * leaves the names as they were). Before genres had their own labels genre was a single colour object; the web still reads one as *. With Tag Styles off, a native-only target, or the default preset and no overrides, every map is empty and the single objects are null. Missing configuration returns 503.

TagStyleOverrides stores a version 2 document, "" when nothing is overridden:

{"v":2,"preset":"glass",
 "groups":{"quality":{"background":"rgba(30, 136, 229, 1)","text":"rgba(255, 255, 255, 1)"}},
 "labels":{"quality:HEVC":{"background":"rgba(239, 108, 0, 1)"},"ageRating:9":{"border":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)"},"status:trending":{"text":"…"}}}

Groups are quality, ageRating, rating, genre, status, language, awards, logos, custom. Custom labels use custom:<label> (up to 24 characters; punctuation-only labels are reserved). Logos labels are logos:provider|company|text. Awards labels are awards:imdbTop250|certifiedFresh|oscar|emmy|letterboxdTop250. Labels are group:label: quality catalog labels, age board ids from the catalog, rating:community|critic|userReview, genre:<genre>, status:added|newMovie|newSeries|newEpisode|trending|new_season|season_premiere|season_finale|series_finale|complete_season|airing_today|airs_date|returns_date|coming_soon|returning|ended|cancelled and language:flag|code|subtitles|countBadge|dual|multi plus lowercase ISO language-code labels (including regional codes). Genre labels are the canonical English genres of js/tags/genre-icons.json, one per icon (genre:action, genre:horror, genre:science fiction, genre:tv movie, genre:game-show, genre:reality-tv, …, 25 in all), plus genre:other for genres outside the table; every spelling and translation of a genre in the table (Sci-Fi, Comédie, Ужасы) takes its canonical genre's label, on the web (data-je-genre) and on native posters alike. scripts/generate_genre_labels.py writes the web table from that file (--check verifies it); native code reads the file itself. The single genre:genre label of documents saved before is read as the genre group's colours (over any stored group colours, which is what every genre chip drew) and is not written again. Fields are background, border, text; language chips take all three fields; only flag images use just the border ring. Chip-code/dual/multi labels override the chip-kind label, then the language group and preset. TagStylePreset is the authoritative preset; the document's own preset mirrors it. Saving validates the document, whichever version it is (leaving out v does not skip the checks): unknown keys, groups, labels or fields, the reserved keys __proto__, constructor and prototype, anything that is not a colour, more than 400 labels or more than 40 KB keep the current styles (logged as a warning); valid documents are stored normalised to rgba(), keys in ordinal order and fields as background, border, text (the Media Tags tab's editor writes that order, so a save comes back unchanged). The fixed-label regression checks that every catalog label, including the language-code labels and all 26 genres, with every colour field at its longest normalised value still fits the 40 KB cap. A version 1 document ({quality:{label:{background,border,color}},age:{boardId:…},rating:{community|critic:…},genre:…}, from before the editor redesign) is still read: each stored label becomes the colours it drew (the stored field, else the built-in colour; rating chips get no border) under the default preset, whatever TagStylePreset says (its genre colour becomes the genre group's), and it is converted to version 2 on the next save.

Catalog (administrator) has quality:[{label,background,color}], age:[{id,background,border,color,ratings,sample}], presets (ids in editor order), groups ({group:[{key,name}]}), genreIcons ({genreLabel: glyph}, the icon each genre label's tile shows; other has the default theaters) and palettes ({preset:{"group:label":{background,border,color}}}, every colour concrete: the preset's colour where it sets one, else the built-in colour; for poster, the colours an example red poster gives every tag but flags) and poster ({worstContrast, example:{background,border,color}}: the lowest text contrast the Poster preset's normalisation can produce over any artwork, and the example colours). It provides shipped defaults and palettes, rather than a user's effective styles.
