Auto Picture-in-Picture Off Tries to open browser PiP when you leave the tab and closes PiP that JE opened when you return. Long Press for 2x Speed (β) Off Hold the video for 500 ms for temporary 2× playback; release or cancel to restore the previous rate. Mouse and touch are supported. Custom Pause Screen On Shows artwork and playback information after idle time while paused. Refresh after changing the toggle. Delay before showing (seconds): 5 Sets the pause-screen idle delay, from 1–60 whole seconds. Updates the running pause screen immediately.

On the pause screen, press Space/Enter or tap the background to resume. × dismisses the overlay for the rest of that pause without resuming. See Enhanced features for the pause screen and playback controls.

Keep playing in Picture-in-Picture

Turn Auto-pause off if you want continuous playback in PiP. Auto-pause and PiP can both run when you leave the tab. PiP needs browser support and an eligible video; the browser may refuse the request.

Details

Auto-resume does not resume a video you had already paused manually before leaving.

Reload after first enabling Long Press for 2x Speed (β). Moving more than ten pixels before the hold activates cancels it. Holding a paused video attempts to start playback.

Pause-screen artwork depends on the item's available images.

docs.title: Auto-Skip Settings
docs.text:
Auto-skip lets you move past intros and outros during web playback. You can choose either type separately for your account.

Open Auto-Skip Settings and turn on the segment types you want to skip.

Setting Default What it does Automatically Skip Intro Off Seeks to the end of an Intro segment. Automatically Skip Outro Off Seeks to the end of an Outro segment.

Intro/outro data required

Auto-skip needs usable Intro/Outro segment data, commonly supplied by Intro Skipper. The panel says Depends on Intro-Skipper Plugin being available.

How it works

JE reads Jellyfin's Media Segments API. It does not need a visible or English-language skip button. Segments without start/end boundaries or shorter than one second are ignored. Failed segment retrieval or an ambiguous playing-item identity can leave auto-skip inactive. If you seek back into a skipped segment, you can watch it without immediately skipping again.

Direct play and HLS work best. Progressive transcoding may not have produced the target yet. These local seeks do not synchronize a SyncPlay group. Outro skipping seeks to the segment end; Jellyfin remains responsible for next-episode autoplay.

docs.title: Subtitle Settings
docs.text:
Make text subtitles easier to read with your preferred colors, size, and position. These are per-user preferences for the web player.

  1. Open Subtitle Settings and choose a preset.
  2. Adjust the preview, or use the color and opacity controls.
  3. To use positioning, set Jellyfin's own subtitle appearance to Custom.

Setting Default What it does Disable Custom Styles Off Uses Jellyfin's subtitle styling instead of JE's overrides. Refresh after changing it. Style Clean White Chooses Clean White, Classic Black Box, Netflix Style, Cinema Yellow, Soft Gray, or High Contrast. Choosing a style replaces custom text/background colors. Text Opaque white (#FFFFFFFF) Sets text color and opacity; the opacity slider runs from 0–255. Background Transparent (#00000000) Sets background color and opacity, also 0–255. Size Normal Chooses Tiny, Small, Normal, Large, Extra Large, or Gigantic. Font Default Chooses Default, Noto Sans, Sans Serif, Typewriter, or Roboto. Text Effect Auto Chooses Auto, None, Shadow, Outline, or Outline + Shadow. Auto adds a shadow with a transparent background and none with an opaque box. Position Horizontal 50%, vertical 85% for newly created settings Click or drag the grid to move the subtitle stack. Both axes are limited to 2–98%.

Subtitle formats

These controls style text subtitles, including the primary and secondary text tracks. They do not restyle ASS/SSA, PGS, VobSub, DVB, or subtitles burned into the video.

See Enhanced features for subtitle previews and rendering limits.

Details

The vertical position locates the subtitle stack's lower edge. The position reset icon sets horizontal 50%, vertical 95%. Missing-value client fallbacks also use 95% vertically.

Roboto uses Roboto Mono. Colors, fonts, and sizes also apply to native browser cues, though their box styling differs.

When you open the panel, the format warning checks the primary subtitle track of the first controllable playing session. Reopen after changing tracks. No warning does not guarantee that the format is supported.

docs.title: Random Button Settings
docs.text:
The header's dice button helps you pick something to watch by opening a random item's details. It does not start playback automatically.

  1. Open Random Button Settings.
  2. Choose your per-user pool under Item Types and Random Source.
  3. Click the header dice button to pick an item.
Setting Default What it does Enable Random Button On Shows the header dice button. Unwatched Only Off Restricts candidates to unplayed movies/episodes or series with unwatched episodes. Movies On Includes movies. Shows On Includes series, and episodes within containers. At least one item type must remain selected. Use the playlist or collection I'm viewing Off Gives the current playlist/collection detail page priority over the pinned source. Everywhere else, pick from Whole library Pins an accessible playlist or collection for other pages. This choice has no admin counterpart. How it works

With current-container selection enabled, a readable playlist or collection on the current detail page takes priority. Otherwise, JE tries your pinned source.

If none is pinned, JE uses the whole library. A missing or invalid pinned source also uses the library, with a notice. If a resolved container's sample has no eligible items, JE goes directly to the whole library with a notice, bypassing the pinned source. Candidate-query errors show an error toast instead.

Container queries use direct children; whole-library queries are recursive. Each query samples at most 100 randomly ordered items. An empty filtered sample does not prove the entire source has no eligible items.

docs.title: UI Settings
docs.text:
Choose the extra information you see on item details and add removal buttons to home rows. These controls are per-user preferences.

Open UI Settings and turn on the options you want.

Setting Default What it does Show Watch Progress Off Adds watch progress to item details. Percentage / Time Watched / Time Remaining Percentage Chooses how Show Watch Progress shows progress. h:m / yd:h:m h:m Selects the time format for time-based progress displays. Show File Sizes Off Shows total file size on item details. Show Audio Languages On Audio language links on item details. Add Remove from Continue Watching & Next Up Buttons Off Adds removal buttons to home rows and keeps your playback position.

Poster tags moved to Media Tags; UI Settings keeps a Media Tags moved to its own section note with an Open button.

How it works

The progress-display selector beneath Show Watch Progress has no separate label.

Row removal can work without the full Hidden Content feature when the administrator enables Enable "Remove from Continue Watching". The relevant Filter Continue Watching / Filter Next Up preferences and Enable Content Hiding must also remain on for server filtering.

To review or manually restore removed entries, the administrator must enable Enable Hidden Content. In its management page:

  • Use Add back to Continue Watching for a Continue Watching-only entry.
  • Use Unhide for Next Up or combined entries.

Resuming clears Continue Watching-only hides. Combined hides retain their Next Up scope. Next Up-only and global hides remain until removed manually. See Content management.

docs.title: Media Tags
docs.text:
Everything about poster tags for your account: the layout, the tag groups, status badges, rules and locked items, and your colour preset. (Administrators set the server defaults on the Media Tags tab of the Jellyfin Enhanced configuration page; the Server tab here links to it.) Each tab does one job; a live preview beside the tabs (a strip under them on a phone) shows the result as you change it. See The Media Tags section for the preview, the phone layout and search.

LayoutGroupsStatus badgesRules & locksColoursServer (administrators) Setting Default What it does Episode thumbnails / List rows → Use a different look Off Optional layout, density, Position pills and chip limit per shape. Use recommended starts with compact bands for thumbnails or compact corners for list images. Locks and rules take precedence. Portrait and square cards, and Native Poster Tags, keep the default look. Layout tiles: Corners, Bands, Caption, Summary, Minimal Corners Your default layout; the line under the tiles describes the selected one. Arrow keys move between tiles. Label density: Full / Compact Full Compact shortens quality labels and hides the critic score next to a community score. Tag size Default (100%) Smaller (85%), Default (100%), Larger (115%) or Largest (130%); scales text, icons, flags and padding on web and native posters. Gap Default Tight (75%), Default (100%) or Roomy (150%) spacing between tags. Shape overrides can inherit or set their own size and gap. Edge spacing: Default / Tight / Flush The administrator's (Default) How far Corners tags sit from the poster edge: 6px, 3px or touching it. Flush tags follow the poster's rounded corners. Settings saved before layouts keep Default until you change it. Hide tags on hover Off Fades poster tags while you hover a card. Show Tags in Native Clients (Experimental) On Shown only while the administrator has Native Poster Tags on. Draws your tags, including Status, into posters for native apps. Corners and Bands are supported; Caption, Summary and Minimal use Corners. Bands follows its profile, limits and density. Show People Tags Off Age, birthplace and deceased status on cast cards. Presets Built-in presets Apply previews a preset's changes first; Share copies it; Save as preset keeps your settings (up to 10, on the server); Import preset adds a shared one; administrators can offer more. Import & export — Export settings downloads or copies your Media Tags settings; Import settings checks a file or pasted text on the server, shows what changes and what is skipped, and applies it with Undo. See Import, export and presets. Setting Default What it does Move up / move down Status, quality, rating, age rating, language, genre, custom Sets the priority order. Higher groups win when space is short. Group switch Off Turns the group's tags on or off. Position Depends on the layout Where the group goes in the selected layout, or Hidden. Corners offers a 3×3 grid with four corners, top/bottom centre, left/right centre and centre. Native Poster Tags use these picks for Corners and Bands. Show up to Genre 3, language 3, custom 3, awards 2, age rating and status 1, quality, rating and logos All How many tags the group shows (1–10, or All for quality and rating). Include Categories on; low-quality sources off Quality: resolution, source, HDR, special format, video format, sound and edition, their stack order and the sound language. Edition defaults on after sound; Include low-quality sources (CAM, TS, TC, SCR) defaults off. Source/edition naming is resolved on the server. Language: Audio and Subtitles (CC marker), Style: Flags / Codes and Audio count badge: Off / Badge only / Badge and flags. Rating: ordered source checkboxes with move buttons, Minimum score, Colour by score and where to show ratings. Status: the Badges button opens Status badges. Custom chips follow the administrator’s rules (see Custom Tags). Language Style / Audio count badge Flags / Off Codes show uppercase language codes with full-name tooltips. Dual means two audio languages, Multi three or more. The badge and included audio/subtitle chips share the language limit, audio first. Language Priority → Follow server policy On Uses the administrator's live language list. Turn off to search by name or ISO code, add up to 12 languages, move them or remove them. An empty personal list has no priorities. Applies to audio/subtitle chips, Dual/Multi counts, Summary and native posters. Language Only show priority languages Follow server Inherit the current strict policy, show only prioritized languages, or keep other languages after them. The administrator's regional-merge setting still applies. Quality Follow server settings — Edition, low-quality sources, the quality category order and Series and seasons show: follow the administrator again, including later changes. Any change to one of them keeps it as your own, even a change back to the administrator's value. Reset to defaults — Restores the administrator's layout, density, positions, order and limits. Group switches and includes stay.

Priority controls pause until their save finishes. A failed save restores the previous policy while keeping other settings changes. Retry the priority edit once the controls become available.

Setting Default What it does Just Added / New releases / Trending / Schedule / Milestones On Which badge families the Status group may show. A poster shows one badge at a time. Series status Off Returning / Ended / Cancelled. Leaving soon Off Leaving in 5d / Leaving soon on items the server will remove (Maintainerr or the administrator's leaving collections). Says needs a Leaving soon source on the server until an administrator sets one. Direct-play warning Off Transcode / Won't direct play on movies and episodes this browser can't play as they are, with the reasons on hover. Web only; checked for cards on screen whose media Jellyfin has already probed (.strm items are always skipped, since Jellyfin probes them on every lookup).

The administrator's two time windows show beside Just Added and New releases; administrators also get a link to change them. Turn the Status group itself on in Groups. Native posters follow these family switches and time windows too; their trending badge requires a TMDB key. A personal web save remembers the date locale and timezone used for native relative dates. Invalid or oversized context values are dropped, retaining the display-language/server-timezone fallback.

Setting Default What it does Rules None In order, the first enabled rule whose conditions (library, type, genre, age rating) all hold gives the card its layout and density. Arrows reorder, On/Off pauses a rule, Edit loads it into the form, Delete removes it. Otherwise Your layout Every other card uses its shape override, if enabled, or your default layout and density; Change goes to the Layout tab. Locked items None The items you gave their own look in their ⋮ menu's Media Tags editor, each with Edit and Unlock, plus Unlock all. Locks always win. Add a rule Library condition, Caption, Compact Up to five conditions, each needing a value; Add rule adds it at the end of the list. Setting Default What it does Tag Colours Server default Shown only when the administrator turns on Let users pick their own preset in Tag Styles. Each tile shows three chips in that preset's colours; colours the administrator changed for a group or a single tag stay on top. Applies right away on the web; posters drawn for native apps follow the next time they load.

Shortcuts to the Media Tags admin tab: Server defaults for new users, Tag colours editor, Tag cache and Native poster tags. Each Open goes straight to that section of it. Other users never get this tab. The admin tab's Server section also exports and imports the server-wide Media Tags settings and lists the Presets for users (Import, export and presets).

See Tags & Badges for the layouts and their complete settings reference, Rules and locked items for how rules match, and One item's look for the per-item editor in an item's ⋮ menu (layout, density, each group's place and limit, size and spacing, Lock this look for me, and for administrators For everyone (server-wide)). It starts from the item’s resolved look, including shape-specific size and limits. Saving from the admin Rules list returns keyboard focus to that item’s Edit button, or its series after a scope move.

docs.title: Hidden Content
docs.text:
Choose where your saved hidden items disappear and where hide buttons appear. This personal section appears only when the administrator enables Hidden Content.

  1. Open Hidden Content and choose the filters and buttons you want.
  2. Click an item's open-eye Hide button to hide it.
  3. Use Manage Hidden Content to review or restore entries and see your hidden-item count.

All controls below are per-user preferences. The matching admin defaults are under Pages → Hidden Content.

Setting Default What it does Enable Content Hiding On Enables filtering for your account while the server feature is available. Show Hide Buttons On Shows hide controls. Turning it off leaves enabled filters working. Show Confirmation Dialog On Asks before hiding an item. Show on Seerr Items On Shows hide buttons on Seerr search/discovery cards. Show in Library Views Off Shows hide buttons on native library/home cards. Show on Detail Pages On Shows hide controls on supported item detail pages. Show on Cast/Actors Off Shows hide controls on cast/actor cards and supports hiding people. Filter Library On Filters native library browsing and supported related detail-page lists. Filter Discovery On Filters Seerr discovery. Filter Search Off Filters Jellyfin and Seerr search results. Filter Calendar On Filters the calendar. Filter Upcoming On Filters upcoming episodes. Filter Recommendations On Filters suggestions and similar/recommended rows. Filter Requests On Filters the Requests page. Filter Next Up On Filters the Next Up home row. Filter Continue Watching On Filters the Continue Watching home row. Hide Collections & Libraries Off Experimental: also allows hiding libraries, collections, and playlists.

Note

Global hides apply across the surfaces whose filters you enable. Search remains visible by default. Hiding changes browsing results; it does not revoke direct access or prevent playback. Experimental container hiding can disrupt browsing.

Details

Button locations and surface filters are under Hide Button Visibility. The experimental control is under Experimental. These preferences are stored in hidden-content.json. See Content management for scope choices and limits.

docs.title: Spoiler Guard
docs.text:
Choose which types of spoilers you want hidden. Your personal choices inherit the administrator's protection policy unless you opt out.

  1. Open Spoiler Guard when its server feature is enabled.
  2. Uncheck a category to opt out. Check it again to inherit the admin policy.
Setting Default What it does TV show descriptions Checked; inherit admin policy Hides protected show descriptions. Episode descriptions Checked; inherit admin policy Hides protected episode descriptions. Episode titles Checked; inherit admin policy Replaces protected episode titles. Chapter names Checked; inherit admin policy Hides protected chapter names. Cast list Checked; inherit admin policy Hides protected cast information. Ratings Checked; inherit admin policy Hides protected community/critic ratings. Air date Checked; inherit admin policy Hides protected air dates. Taglines Checked; inherit admin policy Hides protected taglines. Tags Checked; inherit admin policy Hides protected metadata tags. Reviews Checked; inherit admin policy Hides reviews in the protected web interface. Seek previews Checked; inherit admin policy Hides trickplay thumbnails while seeking through protected unwatched episodes and movies. Advanced per-category reveals Checked; inherit admin policy Uses the admin's enabled advanced reveals; unchecking restores stricter uniform protection. Don't ask me to confirm when turning Spoiler Guard off Off Skips the disable-confirmation dialog.

See Spoiler Guard settings for the admin controls and full protection rules.

Details

Category rows appear only when the administrator enables that category. Advanced per-category reveals appears only when advanced mode is enabled. These per-user preferences are stored in spoilerblur.json.

docs.title: Language Settings
docs.text:
Choose the language of JE's interface. This does not set your audio or subtitle language.

  1. Open Language Settings and choose Display Language.
  2. Wait about 1.5 seconds for the page to reload.
Setting Default What it does Display Language Auto Uses Jellyfin's resolved document language, or lets you choose a JE translation. New accounts start from the administrator's Default UI Language.

To clear this browser's JE translations, click Clear Translation Cache. The page reloads after about two seconds and keeps your feature preferences and language choice. See Other settings for server cache controls.

How it works

Changing Display Language saves the server preference and this browser's user-language key. An existing browser language key takes priority during translation loading. Changing the preference on another device does not automatically replace it. Choose the desired language in this browser if it continues to use an older choice.

Clear Translation Cache removes this browser's JE translation-cache entries. It differs from the server's Refresh Translation Cache scheduled task, which signals invalidation on clients' next load. Clearing does not guarantee a newer translation: bundled translations are tried first.

docs.title: About
docs.text:
Check About to see your installed plugin version. This section has no settings.

Choose Release Notes to fetch the latest GitHub release, or Contribute to open the project repository.

Details

Release Notes needs browser access to GitHub. The latest release may differ from your installed version.

docs.title: Feature Toggles
docs.text:
Use the admin configuration page to turn server features on and set starting preferences for users. You can search across tabs to find a control.

  1. Open Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced.
  2. Select the appropriate tab, or use Search settings... to find controls across tabs. Clear the search to restore normal navigation.
  3. Change the controls and click Save Settings.
  4. Refresh affected web clients to load the new configuration.

Descriptions shows or hides explanations. Section jumps, previews, and navigation do not save edits; watch the unsaved indicator before leaving.

How it works

The tabs are Overview, Display, Media Tags, Elsewhere & Reviews, Playback, Pages, Extras, Keyboard, Services, Seerr, *arr, Admin, Credits, and Docs. The sidebar groups them and lists each tab's cards (for Media Tags, its sections) underneath. The configuration page uses #/configurationpage?name=Jellyfin%20Enhanced, and &tab=<id> opens a tab (&jeSection=media-tags&tab=groups a section of Media Tags). The Media Tags tab saves each change as you make it, so it has no Save Settings; Save Settings on the other tabs never changes a Media Tags setting. See Tags & badges.

Some server effects happen immediately. Page integrations can have additional requirements, described below.

Overview contains Service Status, Optional Dependencies, Features, and Quick Actions. Status/feature cards take you to their configuration. Re-test all service connections runs service checks. Connection and URL-mapping tests are also available in their integration sections. Clear all client tag caches is a cache action, described in Tags & Badges.

What's new in v{version}: or What's new since you last checked: links to newly detected settings, with New in v{version} badges and release links. Dismiss acknowledges the shared server baseline; it does not enable features. Undismissed additions keep their first-detected version across releases.

A fresh installation establishes the current baseline. Existing plugin data can trigger the bundled 12.2.0.0 baseline when no acknowledgment exists. This is settings discovery rather than a complete release history.

docs.title: Server defaults and overwriting personal settings
docs.text:
Admin Display/Playback preferences generally supply starting values when a user settings file is missing. Existing personal values take precedence; ordinary Save Settings does not keep enforcing those defaults.

To change existing users, a setting that users also hold personally (marked with a small people icon) shows a banner in its card when you change it. Apply the above copies only the listed settings to every user. Apply all plugin settings replaces all personal preferences with the admin values.

To replace all existing preferences from the Overview instead:

  1. Set and save the intended defaults.
  2. Choose Overview → Quick Actions → Apply all plugin settings to every user.
  3. Confirm the action.

Warning

This action replaces personal customizations. Users must refresh and reapply choices they want to keep. It also resets personal-only values such as custom subtitle colors/position, the pinned random source, and last-opened section.

For the broader storage and backup reference, see Settings overview.

How it works

Server feature switches, such as Enable Hidden Content, control availability independently of a user's saved choice. Disabled child controls need their parent feature enabled.

After confirmation, the overwrite action saves the current form and synchronizes managed Custom Tabs entries. It replaces general settings for users with known JE data folders. It resets Hidden Content preferences while keeping hidden items. It also resets existing Spoiler Guard preferences to inherit the admin policy while keeping protected-title lists. Shortcut overrides in shortcuts.json remain.

In this version, the overwrite path resets watch-progress mode/time format to Percentage/h:m, even if the corresponding admin defaults differ.

docs.title: Display defaults
docs.text:
Choose the starting information new users see on item details. Users can override these admin preferences in UI Settings.

Open Display → UI Preferences and set the starting values:

Setting Default What it does Show watch progress Off Starts Show Watch Progress enabled for new users. Watch Progress Default Percentage Starts the personal display at Percentage, Time Watched, or Time Remaining. Watch Progress Time Format h:m Starts the personal time format at h:m or yd:h:m. Show file sizes Off Starts Show File Sizes enabled. Show available audio languages on item detail page On Starts Show Audio Languages enabled; users override it in UI Settings. Enable "Remove from Continue Watching" Off Starts Add Remove from Continue Watching & Next Up Buttons enabled.

Under Display → Icons & Theme, these are server settings with no personal-panel counterpart:

Setting Default What it does Use Icons in UI On Uses icons in JE's interface. Icon Style Emoji Chooses Emoji, Lucide Icons, or Material UI Icons.

Under Display → Default Language, choose the starting interface language:

Setting Default What it does Default UI Language System Default Supplies the initial personal Display Language. Users can choose their own language or Auto.

Display → Spoiler Guard is covered by Spoiler Guard settings. Display → Awards and MDBList Ratings are covered by Other settings.

docs.title: Playback defaults
docs.text:
Set starting playback preferences for your users, including tab switching, auto-skip, and subtitles. Users can override the personal preferences in Playback Settings, Auto-Skip Settings, and Subtitle Settings.

Open Playback → Player Behaviour to set these starting preferences. The playback-start rating badge is a server setting with no personal toggle.

Setting Default What it does Auto-pause on tab switch On Starts personal Auto-pause enabled. Auto-resume on tab switch Off Starts personal Auto-resume enabled. Auto Picture-in-Picture on tab switch Off Starts personal Auto Picture-in-Picture enabled. Browser restrictions still apply. Long press/hold for 2x speed β Off Starts personal Long Press for 2x Speed (β) enabled. Supports mouse and touch. Enable Custom Pause Screen On Starts personal Custom Pause Screen enabled. Show Age Rating When Playback Starts Off Shows rating information when playback starts. No personal-panel toggle.

Player rating chips have a separate admin server control under Media Tags → Groups → Rating:

Setting Default What it does Show Rating in Video Player On Adds community/critic rating chips beside the player's time information. Uses the server setting and has no personal-panel toggle.

Under Playback → Auto-Skip, choose starting preferences for Auto-Skip Settings:

Setting Default What it does Auto-skip Intro Off Starts Automatically Skip Intro enabled. Requires usable Intro segment data. Auto-skip Outro Off Starts Automatically Skip Outro enabled. Requires usable Outro segment data.

Under Playback → Subtitles, choose starting preferences for Subtitle Settings:

Setting Default What it does Disable Custom Subtitle Styles by default Off Starts Disable Custom Styles enabled. Users can override it. Default Subtitle Style Clean White Supplies the initial Style. Default Subtitle Size Normal Supplies the initial Size. Default Subtitle Font Default Supplies the initial Font. Default Subtitle Text Effect Auto Supplies the initial Text Effect.

See Subtitle Settings for choices and format limits.

Under Playback → Shortcuts Panel & Toast Timing, set these server timings. Use Preview autoclose and Preview toast to try them:

Setting Default What it does Shortcuts Panel Autoclose Delay (ms) 15000 Sets how long the Enhanced panel stays open with the pointer outside it. Toast Notification Duration (ms) 1500 Sets JE toast duration. Details

Show Age Rating When Playback Starts shows the official rating, up to three recognized advisory tags, and up to three genres for five seconds when playback starts. Episodes can fall back to series metadata.

There is no admin form input for the pause-screen delay. Its server configuration default is five seconds; users have Delay before showing (seconds):. Custom subtitle colors and position also have no admin form inputs.

docs.title: Random button defaults
docs.text:
Set the dice button's starting pool for new users. Users can override all five preferences in Random Button Settings.

Open Display → Random Button and choose the starting values:

Setting Default What it does Enable Random Button On Starts the header dice button enabled. Show unwatched only Off Starts Unwatched Only enabled. Include movies On Starts Movies selected. Include shows On Starts Shows selected. Scope to the current playlist or collection Off Starts Use the playlist or collection I'm viewing enabled.

Users choose their own pinned source; no admin control sets it. See Random Button Settings for source priority and sampling limits.

docs.title: Keyboard configuration
docs.text:
Set the server's keyboard bindings, which users inherit until they choose personal overrides. You can also disable ordinary JE shortcuts.

  1. Open Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts.
  2. Click a key and press a combination. Del disables the server binding; Backspace restores its stock key.
  3. Save your admin edits.
Setting Default What it does Disable Keyboard Shortcuts Off Disables ordinary JE shortcuts and hides the personal Shortcuts section. You can still open the panel with ?.

The editable action labels and stock keys match the Shortcuts table, except Jump to % of video, which is not in the admin recorder.

Details

Personal overrides remain in effect until users reset them in their own editor. Personal Backspace restores the saved administrator binding, which may differ from the stock key.

docs.title: Page entry points
docs.text: Enable the page under Pages, choose its placement, and click Save Settings. Bookmarks, Hidden Content, Activity, and Catch Up controls are listed below. Follow JE Pages & Tabs for native Home links, Plugin Pages registration, and automatic or manual Custom Tabs setup.

docs.title: Bookmarks
docs.text:
Bookmarks save positions within videos so you can return to them later. The bookmark library lets you manage those saved positions.

  1. Under Pages → Bookmarks, enable the server feature and choose an entry point.
  2. Create a bookmark in the player or with Bookmark Current Time.

These are admin server settings. There is no personal bookmark master toggle in the Enhanced panel.

Setting Default What it does Enable Bookmarks Feature On Enables bookmark tools and management. Add Bookmarks as a native Home tab Off Adds the built-in Bookmarks Home tab. Use Plugin Pages for Bookmarks Library Off Exposes the bookmark library through Plugin Pages. Use Custom Tabs for Bookmarks Off Enables the bookmark library's Custom Tabs embed. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Creates the matching managed Custom Tabs entry on save.

Custom Tabs is optional. See Smart Bookmarks for editing, timeline markers, and management.

Details

Bookmark data is saved per account on the server in bookmark.json. The interface has no export/import operation.

docs.title: Hidden Content administration
docs.text:
Enable Hidden Content so users can manage their own hidden lists. When allowed, administrators can also inspect and edit other users' lists.

  1. Open Pages → Hidden Content.
  2. Enable the server feature and choose page access; expand Admin Controls to set administrator access to other users' hidden content.
  3. Under More Settings, set the starting personal preferences.

Admin server settings:

Setting Default What it does Enable Hidden Content Off Enables Hidden Content, its management page, and its personal panel section. Add Hidden Content as a native Home tab Off Adds the built-in Hidden Content Home tab. Use Plugin Pages for Hidden Content Off Exposes the page through Plugin Pages. Use Custom Tabs for Hidden Content Off Enables its Custom Tabs embed. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Creates the matching managed Custom Tabs entry on save. Let admins view and manage other users' hidden content On Adds another-user selection to management. Viewing another account starts read-only; Edit enables changes on its behalf.

Under More Settings, these admin values supply starting values for the matching personal Hidden Content controls. Saving new defaults leaves existing personal copies intact.

Setting Default What it does Hidden Content enabled by default On Sets Enable Content Hiding. Show "Hide" buttons by default On Sets Show Hide Buttons. Show confirmation dialog before hiding On Sets Show Confirmation Dialog. Show "Hide" button on Seerr search results On Sets Show on Seerr Items. Show "Hide" button on item details pages On Sets Show on Detail Pages. Show "Hide" button on library / home cards Off Sets Show in Library Views. Show "Hide" button on cast / actor cards Off Sets Show on Cast/Actors. Filter Library & details pages On Sets Filter Library. Filter Search results Off Sets Filter Search. Filter Continue Watching On Sets Filter Continue Watching. Filter Next Up On Sets Filter Next Up. Filter Upcoming episodes On Sets Filter Upcoming. Filter Suggestions / recommendations On Sets Filter Recommendations. Filter Discovery On Sets Filter Discovery. Filter Calendar On Sets Filter Calendar. Filter Requests page On Sets Filter Requests. Allow hiding collections, libraries, and playlists (experimental) Off Sets Hide Collections & Libraries. Experimental container hiding can disrupt browsing. Details

The server master defaults to Off even though personal hiding defaults to On. The personal controls and browsing limits are separate from the row-removal preference in Display → UI Preferences.

docs.title: Activity Feed
docs.text:
Activity shows watching history, favorites, and reviews, with an optional live-stream section. You can open titles or artwork to view their details.

  1. Enable the feature under Pages → Activity Feed and configure an entry point.
  2. Open Activity and browse Active Streams, Watch History, and Reviews. Favorites share Reviews.
  3. Use Refresh to reload stored activity. Partial watches show progress; completed watches use completion wording.

All settings below are admin server settings, with no personal-panel counterparts.

The disabled Use Plugin Pages and Use Custom Tabs controls require their companion plugins.

Setting Default What it does Enable Activity Feed Off Enables the feed and its watched/favorite collection. Turning it off retains saved activity. Show recently watched On Collects and shows qualifying stopped or completed playback. Show recently favorited On Collects and shows favorites. Unfavoriting removes the saved entry. Show recently reviewed On Includes reviews from the current User Reviews store. Non-admins only see their own activity Off Regular users only see their own watched, favorited and reviewed entries; administrators still see everyone. Show Active Streams section On Adds live sessions when the separate Active Streams feature and viewer permissions allow them. Add Activity as a native Home tab Off Adds the built-in Activity Home tab. Use Plugin Pages Off Exposes Activity through Plugin Pages. Use Custom Tabs Off Enables the Activity Custom Tabs embed. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Creates the matching managed Custom Tabs entry on save.

For the live section, also configure these admin server settings under Extras → Active Streams:

Setting Default What it does Active Streams Header Widget Off Enables the header widget and live-session data used by the feed. Show widget to non-admins Off Permits authenticated non-admins to read live sessions.

Stored watched/favorite/review entries respect viewer library access. Active Streams has separate access rules and can show sessions for items outside a viewer's library access. See Other settings for the widget's full behavior.

How it works

Show recently watched collects playback stopped at a position of at least 5% of known runtime, plus playback Jellyfin reports completed. The 5% threshold measures stopped playback position, not time spent watching.

The usual request returns up to 50 merged entries with no UI pagination. Watched/favorite storage in activity.json is capped at 500 entries. Rewatches update the timestamp while retaining maximum progress and completion.

Elsewhere & Reviews → User Reviews → Hide reviews from hidden users and Hide reviews from disabled users both default to On. They also filter activity authors, with admin/self exceptions. User Reviews runs independently. Disabling Activity Feed stops watched/favorite collection, but reviews written while it is off can appear when the feed returns. See Elsewhere & Reviews Settings for those shared review controls.

Active Streams Header Widget enables the Active Streams data endpoint as well as the header widget. The feed's live section refreshes every 15 seconds while the document is visible. Stored history does not use that polling. The header widget refreshes on initialization, opening, and manual refresh.

docs.title: Catch Up
docs.text:
Catch Up gives you swipeable cards for unwatched movies and shows. Use them to mark items watched, dismiss them, add them to your watchlist, or open their details.

  1. Enable the feature under Pages → Catch Up and configure an entry point.
  2. Open Catch Up and choose Movies or Shows.
  3. Swipe right to mark watched, left to dismiss, up to add to the watchlist, or down to open details. Buttons and arrow keys provide the same actions.
  4. Press Backspace to rewind when an undo is available.

All settings below are admin server settings.

Setting Default What it does Enable Catch Up Off Enables decks of unwatched items accessible to each user. Add Catch Up as a native Home tab Off Adds the built-in Catch Up Home tab. Use Plugin Pages Off Exposes Catch Up through Plugin Pages. Use Custom Tabs Off Enables the Catch Up Custom Tabs embed. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Creates the matching managed Custom Tabs entry on save. Record Catch Up activity On Saves reported actions for administrators while Catch Up is enabled. Turning it off stops new records; existing history remains readable.

Dismissals stay in this browser for your account, separate from server-synced Hidden Content. Reloading keeps them. Clear their browser storage or use an available rewind to reverse them.

Administrators can open Activity to view Feed or Summary, even with recording disabled. Use All users, Search titles, and action chips to filter Feed; those filters do not affect Summary. Refresh reloads the selected view and Hide closes it.

See Enhanced features for the full gesture workflow and API reference for event routes.

How it works

The watchlist uses Jellyfin's Likes flag. Decks sample random batches of 40 items, excluding dismissed, already-seen, and imageless cards. They do not sort newest first. Nothing more to show here. can mean a batch produced no eligible new cards.

A show's season picker appears only with at least two regular seasons; specials are excluded. Shows with fewer regular seasons are marked watched directly.

The selected deck mode is remembered locally for the browser. Switching decks or restarting resets the queue, seen set, and undo history.

The open admin activity panel refreshes every ten seconds and docks at widths of at least 1100 pixels. Narrower screens use a dialog.

Logs contain open, undo, and failed actions as well as swipes. They are client-reported actions, not proof of viewing. Feed requests up to 300 matching events. Summary counts distinct surviving user/title actions not marked failed, removes recorded undos, and lists up to 15 top titles per action.

The server retains catchup-log.jsonl and catchup-log.1.jsonl in the plugin configuration folder. It rotates before the next append once the live file exceeds 5 MiB.

docs.title: Tags: Quality, Genre, Language, Rating, Age Rating, Status, Awards, Logos, Custom, People
docs.text: All tag settings have moved to Tags & Badges: personal Media Tags controls, the admin Media Tags tab's defaults, quality categories/order, language preferences, rating scopes, custom tag rules, people/review badges, hover behavior, and Tag Styles.

docs.title: Custom tag rules
docs.text: Media Tags → Groups → Custom (the configuration page's Media Tags tab) turns Jellyfin tags and collections into poster chips: up to 20 rules of match type, name, label and optional icon, plus Enable Custom Tags and its Position as defaults for users. Colour the labels under Tag Styles → Custom. See Custom Tags.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: For personal tag choices, open Media Tags. Administrators use the configuration page's Media Tags tab. See Tags & Badges for exact labels, defaults, and configuration instructions.

docs.title: Status Tags badge groups
docs.text: Under Media Tags → Status badges, the eight personal switches are Just Added, New releases (New Movie / New Series / New Episode), Trending, Schedule (Airing Today / Airs / Returns / Coming Soon), Milestones (New Season / Premiere / Finale / Complete Season), Series status (Returning / Ended / Cancelled), Leaving soon (Maintainerr or leaving collections) and Direct-play warning (Transcode / Won't direct play, web only). The first five default on; the last three off. The administrator sets the Leaving soon source (Maintainerr URL and API key, or existing collection names, and how often it is read) in the Status badges section of the Media Tags admin tab; see Leaving soon and Direct-play warning. Administrators set starting defaults and the two shared day windows in the Status badges section of that tab. Finale and series schedule enrichment require a TMDB key; Jellyfin date badges work without one. Compact density shortens long milestone labels. See Status Tags for sources and first-match priority by card type.

docs.title: Logo Tags
docs.text: The Logos row on the Groups tab of Media Tags turns the group on (off by default) and sets its position and Show up to. What the logo shows is the administrator's choice under Media Tags → Groups → Logos: Movies show (streaming service, studio or no logo), Series show (network, streaming service or no logo), Streaming region and Logos per title (1 or 2). Logos need the TMDB API key for images; without one, names are shown. See Logo Tags.

docs.title: Server-Side Tag Cache
docs.text: Server cache settings, library exclusions, browser fallback persistence, Clear All Client Caches, and Admin → Tag Cache → Rebuild Server Tag Cache are covered in Tags & Badges.

docs.title: Audio Language Tags
docs.text: The controls under Display → Audio Language Tags and the Sync Audio Language Tags to Jellyfin task are covered in Tags & Badges.

docs.title: Native Poster Tags (Experimental)
docs.text: The admin Media Tags tab's controls and personal Show Tags in Native Clients (Experimental) are covered in Tags & Badges, including eligible clients, exclusions, and refresh requirements.

docs.title: Settings in other areas
docs.text:
Use these references for settings owned by other feature areas:

  • Seerr and Pages → Seerr Recommendations Page: Seerr settings.
  • *arr, Pages → Calendar Page, and the download parts of Pages → Requests Page: *arr settings. Request controls are also covered in Seerr settings.
  • Elsewhere, TMDB Reviews, Release Dates, and User Reviews: Elsewhere & Reviews Settings. Written reviews have no separate personal review-tag switch.
  • Display → Spoiler Guard: Spoiler Guard settings.
  • Display → Awards / MDBList Ratings, other Extras options, and Admin maintenance, analytics, developer, and cache controls: Other settings.

docs.title: Documentation in the dashboard
docs.text:
Read the hosted documentation from the dashboard's Docs tab. This tab has no enable switch.

Open Docs to load Documentation from the GitHub Pages site, or choose Open in new tab.

Details

The tab needs connectivity from your browser; it is not an offline copy bundled with the plugin. It loads the document when first opened and retains it when you switch tabs.

If no iframe load event arrives within eight seconds, a fallback message and link replace it. Open in new tab is always an alternative.

docs.title: Awards poster group
docs.text: Media Tags → Groups → Awards enables chart and winner chips, with the usual position, priority and cap controls (default two). Existing users start off. Administrators first enable Awards under Display → Media Tags → Awards Tags, choose ribbons, configure the two MDBList lists and a freshness interval (24 hours), and run Refresh Awards Tags. IMDb/Letterboxd charts and Certified Fresh require the server MDBList key; Wikidata Oscar/Emmy wins do not. Native posters follow the same group preference. See Awards Tags.

docs.title: Quality stream display
docs.text: In Media Tags → Groups → Quality, the Sound, Video codec and HDR display modes independently choose Highest only (the unchanged default) or All distinct values. Minimum resolution to show filters resolution chips below Off / 720p / 1080p / 4K; Hide SDR removes SDR exposed by All HDR mode. Each field offers Server default; Follow server settings also restores these five overrides and the technical category switches/orders. Explicit choices stay personal even if they equal the server defaults. Administrator defaults live on the dedicated Media Tags → Groups → Quality page. The Quality group limit and Compact labels apply to the resulting chips, including the existing layout overflow count. See quality display and aggregation.

docs.title: Technical poster facts
docs.text:
Media Tags → Groups → Quality → Include adds Runtime, Aspect ratio and Frame rate, all off initially, with the usual stacking-order controls. The administrator sets their new-user defaults on the Media Tags admin tab, Groups → Quality. Full/Compact density changes duration and ratio labels. Media Tags → Status badges → Scenes is also off initially and allows Post-credits/Mid-credits movie badges once the administrator enables the family and configures TMDB. Language subtitle chips automatically use SDH for hearing-impaired tracks when Include → Subtitles is on; no extra language switch is required. See Tags & badges.

The Media Tags group editor hides Show up to for Status and Age rating, and for Logos when the administrator allows only one logo. Other groups keep their limit control.

Changing Quality includes or display modes in Media Tags keeps the dialog frame and preview in place, preserving the inner pane scroll and the changed control's focus.

In Compact quality labels, AC-3 is DD 5.1 and E-AC-3 is DD+ 5.1; Full shows Dolby Digital 5.1 / Dolby Digital+ 5.1. Flush edge styling includes overflow tabs and keeps styled Rating/Awards rings inside the chip on inward sides. Single-chip limits remain effective presentation limits; valid saved caps round-trip unchanged.

Series and season quality policies preserve version-0 audio labels in Highest and All modes, including preferred-language summaries. Editing an unrelated preference leaves the audio vocabulary unchanged.

In the Corners tag layout, left-centre and right-centre groups use the available poster width, sharing it when both sides are occupied. The first chip remains visible even on a narrow poster; long labels use an ellipsis, and +N counts later chips.

When a first chip needs an ellipsis in Corners, only its text shrinks: Custom icons, rating logos and the chip’s height and inward Flush borders stay in place. Awards and Language poster links use the same constraint on their inner chip.

Media Tags live previews react to each sample’s pointer hover or keyboard focus. Hover pins every sample for touch comparison; Resting releases that pin. Tag sizes show percentage values. Language code, CC/SDH and Dual/Multi chips follow the Language Tag Styles colours, including Poster artwork colours.

docs.title: Tags & Badges
docs.text:
See quality, genres, audio languages, scores, age classifications, what is new or trending, and where a title streams or which network or studio made it while browsing your library. You can choose which badges appear, pick a layout for them (corners, bands, a caption below the poster, a summary pill or a minimal set), set their order and limits, and change their colors. People Tags add age and birthplace information to cast cards.

The optional tag groups are enabled for this example; every group starts off.

docs.title: Set up your tags
docs.text:
You can choose tags for your own account. If you administer the server, you can also set the starting values for users.

How to use — personal preferences:

  1. Open the Jellyfin Enhanced panel from the user profile menu on Jellyfin 12 or the sidebar on 10.11. You can also press ?.
  2. Select Media Tags and choose your tags on its tabs (see The Media Tags section). Changes save automatically to your Jellyfin account on the server.
  3. Refresh another open client to load changes you made elsewhere.

How to use — admin defaults:

  1. Open Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced and select the Media Tags tab in the sidebar (under Appearance, after Display). Its sections are listed under it: Overview, Layout defaults, Groups, Rules, Colours, Status badges and Server. On a phone, open the page's menu, or use the row of section chips at the top of the tab. The Media Tags card on the Display tab opens it too. A link can open a section directly: #/configurationpage?name=Jellyfin%20Enhanced&jeSection=media-tags&tab=<id> (overview, layout, groups, rules, colours, badges, server; on Groups add &group=quality and so on). The old address #/configurationpage?name=JellyfinEnhancedMediaTags&tab=<id> still works and goes there.
  2. Choose your settings. Each change saves on its own, so the tab needs no Save Settings. The line on the first card's header (on a phone, at the end of the section chips) says Saving…, then All changes saved. If a save fails, a bar at the bottom of the settings says Not saved with the settings it could not save and Retry. Those changes stay waiting while you move between sections, other tabs and links; the tab's sidebar entry shows a dot until they are saved. If they still cannot be saved when you leave the settings, it offers to take you back. Saving the other tabs (Save Settings, Apply to all users) waits for these changes and never undoes them. Signing out, or switching to another server, drops changes that were not saved; the next administrator to sign in never sees them, and an answer to that offer given after the switch takes no one back. Only the settings you change are saved, so another administrator's changes elsewhere are kept. If someone else changed the same setting since you opened the page, the bar says Changed elsewhere with both values of each setting and offers Keep mine or Take theirs (for one setting, Keep or Use ).
  3. Refresh affected web clients to load the changes.

The Media Tags tab gathers every server-wide tag setting, laid out like the personal Media Tags settings, with a live preview of the cards a brand-new account would see. Its enabled groups follow the current server defaults, including changes awaiting a save, independently of the groups you use on your own account. The preview uses the saved server Tag Styles (refreshed after each Colours change is saved), not the colours your own account uses:

Tab What it holds Overview Which tag groups new users start with (select one to open it), the default look, the server tag cache (items cached, last change, Rebuild cache), Native Poster Tags and tag colours at a glance Layout defaults Default layout, Label density, Tag size, Tag gap and Edge spacing, each group's order, limit and position under Group placement (nine anchors for Corners, the layout's slots otherwise; Reorder groups shows the order buttons), Card shapes for episode thumbnails and list rows, Hide tags on hover, No tags on the search page, and Apply defaults to all users Groups The Tag groups card: one row per group (Quality, Genre, Language, Rating, Age Rating, Status, Awards, Logos, Custom, People) with a summary of its choice and its switch for new users; Edit opens its server settings (Quality's display and audio-language options under Display behaviour and Audio language defaults) Rules The default tag look rules: a list with Edit, the same add/edit form as each user's own Rules & locks (one to five conditions, then the look), and Edit as JSON; and the server-wide item looks with Edit and remove; How user-locked looks work explains users' own locks Colours The Tag Styles editor Status badges The badge families new users start with, the Just added and New release windows, and whether the TMDB key is set Server Server-side tag cache, library exclusions, Rebuild cache, browser cache options and Native Poster Tags

Apply defaults to all users

Apply defaults to all users (Overview tab) copies every saved Jellyfin Enhanced default, not only Media Tags, into every user's settings, replacing what they chose. It asks first and cannot be undone. Reset all colours and deleting a rule can be undone for a few seconds from the message at the bottom of the page.

Tables below show factory defaults. Rows marked “Admin / personal” give both exact labels for the same preference. Most admin defaults become the starting values for new personal settings. Saved personal values take precedence, so changing a server default does not overwrite a user's choice.

Hover hiding starts off

Hide tags on hover follows the admin value for new users, and overwriting personal settings applies it too.

docs.title: The Media Tags section
docs.text:
Every personal poster tag setting lives in one section of the panel, Media Tags, between UI Settings and Hidden Content. Its tabs each do one job, and a live preview beside them shows the result as you change things.

Tab What you set there Layout Your default look: one tile per layout with a line describing the selected one, Label density (Full / Compact), Tag size, Gap, per-shape looks for Episode thumbnails and List rows, and the quick switches Hide tags on hover, Show Tags in Native Clients (Experimental) (only while the administrator has Native Poster Tags on), Show People Tags. Groups The tag groups in priority order: move buttons, the on/off switch, and per group its position, Show up to and Include choices, plus Reset to defaults. The Status row's Badges button opens the next tab. Status badges Which status badges the Status group may show: Just Added, New releases, Trending, Schedule, Milestones, Series status, Leaving soon and Direct-play warning, each with a sample badge. The two time windows the administrator chose are shown beside Just Added and New releases. Status position and limit in Groups goes back to the Status row. Rules & locks Your rules and locked items on the left, the Add a rule form on the right. Colours Your Tag Colours preset, one tile per preset with sample chips in its real colours (a quality, a status and a rating chip, and a genre icon: the first genre the administrator coloured). Only shown while the administrator lets users pick a preset. Server Administrators only: shortcuts to Server defaults for new users, the Tag colours editor, the Tag cache and Native poster tags, each opening its section of the Media Tags admin tab. Other users never get this tab.

The live preview draws four sample cards with the same layout code and tag styles as your library: a movie poster, a series poster, an episode still and a 92px list row. Each says where its look comes from (Default, 🔒 Locked, Server-wide, Rule N or a shape look), decided the same way as for real cards: the series stands in for your most recently locked item and the episode for the first enabled rule, so a lock or rule change shows at once. Resting / Hover switches to what Summary and Minimal reveal on hover. While you edit a group, its chips are outlined and the others dimmed. Overflowing chips show as +N, as on real cards.

The live preview samples respond to pointer hover and keyboard focus to demonstrate genre expansion, reveal lists and hide-on-hover. Library genre-name reveal and hover hiding retain their pointer-hover behavior; keyboard reveal in the previews stays scoped to the samples. Hover pins all samples in that state, including on touch screens; Resting releases the pin while the pointed or focused sample stays active. This applies to the hub, administrator preview and item editor.

On a phone the section fills the screen: the tabs use short names (Badges, Rules), and the preview folds into a one-line strip under them. The strip names the sample that your current edit affects (the episode on Rules & locks, the series for schedule badges) and lists its chips, the edited group's first; tap Preview to unfold the full preview.

The panel's Search settings… box finds every Media Tags control by its label (for example Trending, Show up to or Move Language up); pick a match to open its tab, and its group if needed, with the control focused. Everything in the section works from the keyboard: arrow keys move between tabs and between tiles, and focus stays on the control you used after a move, a delete or an unlock. UI Settings keeps a short Media Tags moved to its own section note with an Open button.

Replacing everyone's preferences

Overview → Quick Actions → Apply all plugin settings to every user replaces saved personal preferences with the current admin values. It also replaces other Enhanced display/playback preferences, so each user would need to reapply their customizations. Read Settings Overview before using it.

docs.title: Where tags appear
docs.text:
You'll see poster badges in library grids, home rows, Jellyfin search results, and supported rows on detail pages. People Tags appear on cast cards instead.

Feature What you see Where it appears Quality Tags Resolution, source, HDR, special format, video codec, sound, edition Supported library cards; series/season quality follows your aggregation policy Genre Tags Genre icons (three by default), with names on hover Supported library cards with genre metadata Language Tags Distinct flags (three by default) or a no-dialogue symbol Supported library cards; cached series/season flags cover their episodes, collection flags cover linked movies and series Rating Tags Community star score and critic percentage Supported library cards User-review chips Average visible review rating, or an optional dash Movie, series, season, and episode cards with a usable review identity Age Rating Tags Official parental/content classification Supported library cards with classification metadata Status Tags One badge: trending, release, schedule, milestone or series status Supported library cards and eligible native posters Logo Tags The streaming service, TV network or studio as a small logo (or its name) Movie, series, season and episode cards; seasons and episodes show their series' logo People Tags Age, age at release, birthplace, deceased styling Cast and guest-cast cards on web item detail pages Audio language links Named audio languages linking to Jellyfin tag lists Movie, series, season, and episode detail pages; control in UI Settings Player badges Scores in the controls; optional age/advisory badge at playback start Jellyfin web video player

Native Poster Tags draw supported poster groups into images for eligible native clients. Their page and row limits differ from web overlays.

Tags need metadata

Each badge needs suitable metadata. A supported card does not guarantee every tag will appear.

Supported cards and locations

Web poster overlays apply to supported movie, series, season, episode, collection (BoxSet), and video cards, including videos in Home Videos/Photos libraries. Detail-page rows include season/episode cards and the series Next Up shelf. Large episode list images can also carry overlays.

The web overlays skip the large artwork in the detail page's information area, cast cards, chapter/scene cards, My Media, modal dialogs, small list images, and plugin/catalog/device/library administration cards. Seerr search and discovery cards do not receive these library tags.

docs.title: Layouts
docs.text:
A layout decides where the poster groups appear and how much of each you see. Pick one for your account; each layout keeps its own arrangement, so you can switch back and forth without losing it. Positions are physical: Top left is the top-left corner of the poster in every interface language, right-to-left ones included, just as native posters draw it; the text inside each chip still reads in its own direction.

How to use — personal preferences:

  1. In Media Tags, on the Layout tab, pick a layout tile, a Label density and, for Corners, an Edge spacing. The live preview shows your layout as you change it.
  2. On the Groups tab, open a group to choose where it goes in that layout and how many tags it shows. Use the arrow buttons to change the priority order.

How to use — admin defaults: on the Media Tags admin tab, open Layout defaults and set the starting layout, density, size, gap, edge spacing, order, positions and limits. Changes save as you make them.

Layout Where tags go Default arrangement Corners (default) Nine anchors: four corners, top/bottom centre, left/right centre and centre; groups sharing an anchor keep their priority order Quality top left, genre and status top right, language bottom left, rating and age rating bottom right Bands A gradient band along the top (first group left, the others right) and one along the bottom that wraps; the middle of the poster stays clear Status and age rating on top; quality, rating and language at the bottom; genre hidden Caption A strip below the poster, between the image and the title, plus a small stack at the poster's top left Status on the poster; quality, rating, age rating and language in the caption; genre hidden Summary One pill at the bottom of the poster with up to three short facts (for example Just Added · 4K DV · ★ 8.1); every group's full chips appear over a dark scrim on hover or keyboard focus Status, quality and rating in the pill; genre, language and age rating on hover Minimal Status at the top left, one coloured dot per quality chip (resolution blue, dynamic range orange, audio green, codec grey), the rating in the bottom-right corner; full chips on hover or focus As listed; genre, language and age rating on hover CornersCentre anchorsBandsCaptionSummaryMinimal

The same four posters and tag groups in every layout.

At left centre or right centre, a group can use the poster's width when the opposite side is empty. With groups on both sides, each keeps half the available width with a gap between them. The first chip at every anchor stays visible; a label too wide for its space is shortened with an ellipsis. The chip keeps its height and icon alignment while its text shortens, including linked Awards and Language chips. A +N chip counts only later chips that do not fit.

Status at left centre (top) and right centre (bottom): the first badge stays visible.

docs.title: Tag size and spacing
docs.text:
On Media Tags → Layout, below Label density, choose Tag size and Gap. The live preview and the cards already on screen update immediately; the choices save to your account.

Setting Choices Default Tag size / admin Default Tag size Smaller (85%), Default (100%), Larger (115%), Largest (130%) Default (100%) Gap / admin Default Gap Tight (75% of the usual spacing), Default (100%), Roomy (150%) Default

Size multiplies the existing card-width sizing, including text, icons, flags, chip padding, summary pills, hover reveals and +N chips. Gap adjusts the spacing between chips and groups in stacks, rows, bands and captions. Larger tags can leave room for fewer chips; the existing limits and overflow fitting still apply. Caption space grows with the chosen size and gap before tag data arrives. Edge insets stay at the chosen 6px, 3px or 0px regardless of size and gap.

Tag size choices are 85%, 100%, 115%, and 130%. The inherited Same as default look option still follows the default size.

Administrators set the starting choices on the plugin's Media Tags page, Layout defaults tab. New users and Apply defaults to all users take those choices. Existing version-0 settings keep their original size and gap, including when saving an unrelated preference. The first layout edit preserves both defaults unless you change one. Reset to defaults restores both admin choices.

An enabled shape override has its own Tag size and Gap selectors. Same as default look inherits that setting independently; choosing Default explicitly keeps 100% even if the default look is larger or roomier. Stored rule/lock shape looks accept the same fields. Native posters follow the account's size and gap in Corners and Bands, and ignore shape overrides.

docs.title: Edge spacing
docs.text:
Edge spacing sets how close the Corners layout puts tags to the poster edge, on all nine anchors:

Edge spacing Distance from the edge Notes Default 6px What Corners always looked like Tight 3px Flush 0px Tags touch the edge, like a tab hanging off the poster: the chip corners against an edge are square, and a tag in a corner follows the poster's own rounded corner. Nothing is drawn outside the poster

Edge spacing sits on the Layout tab below Tag size and Gap.

Flush chips have no visible border or shadow on the sides touching an edge; inward borders and shadows remain. Genre chips follow the same rule, with a flat side against the edge, and still show their name on hover. Language flags keep their shape. Top-centre tabs meet top: 0 with square top corners, and bottom-centre tabs meet bottom: 0 with square bottom corners. If a progress bar is present, bottom centre meets its top edge without a gap. Top centre first narrows to the gap between corner indicators and moves below them only when that gap cannot fit its first chip. Tight and Default retain their existing indicator and progress gaps. The other layouts have their own spacing and ignore it. Native Poster Tags use the selected inset in Corners; Bands retains its own 6px inset, including for overflow chips. Edge spacing applies to every Corners card, including shape overrides; size and gap may be overridden independently for each shape.

Native Flush uses the same touching-edge treatment and centre-row indicator fallback. A native image request does not provide the app's progress-bar geometry; callers with known geometry can supply it to the layout planner. Native apps drawing their own progress overlays still control that placement.

Flush at 5×: the top-centre Status tab sits on the edge beside Jellyfin's count bubble; the bottom-left stack shows the compact DD+ 5.1 label.

Flush and rounded posters

Flush tags are clipped to the poster's rounded corners rather than being given a radius of their own, so a corner tag takes exactly the curve your theme gives the poster.

docs.title: Episode thumbnails and list rows
docs.text:
On Layout, turn on Use a different look under Episode thumbnails or List rows. Each shape has its own layout, label density, group positions and chip limits. Use recommended restores these starting arrangements:

Shape Recommended look Episode thumbnails and backdrop cards Bands, Compact: status and age rating on top, quality and rating below, language and genre hidden Large list images Corners, Compact: quality top left, status top right, rating bottom right, each limited to two chips; the other groups hidden

Both switches start off. Switching one off uses your default look again. Portrait posters and square cards (including music and people) use the default look. Jellyfin's card classes determine the shape first; otherwise the image's rendered aspect ratio does (wider than 1.2:1 is landscape; square cards count as portrait), measured again whenever the card's width or height changes.

The choice for each card is your item lock → the administrator's item look → first matching rule → shape override → default. A lock, item look or rule takes precedence over the general shape settings. Stored rules and locks may also contain their own shape looks through the API; the rule editor continues to edit layout and density only.

The episode and list samples in the live preview follow their own shape settings. Caption on list rows still puts caption chips on the image; choose another layout to avoid this fallback. Native Poster Tags draw on poster images only and ignore shape overrides.

Shape chip limits run from 1 to 10, then All. From All, press − to return to 10; at 1, − is disabled.

Administrators can choose Same look as posters or the recommended look for each shape under Layout defaults → Card shapes on the Media Tags admin tab. This seeds new users and applies when overwriting personal settings. Existing version-0 documents keep their old look until an explicit edit; merely loading or saving unrelated preferences does not enable overrides.

docs.title: Tag groups: order, position, limits
docs.text:
Each group has a row on the Groups tab, highest priority first. Groups higher in the list win when space is short: they stack nearest the edge of a shared corner, come first in a band or the caption, and take the summary pill's three places first. The row shows where the group goes in the selected layout and how many tags it shows (for example Bottom row · up to 3); the switch on the right turns the group on or off.

Open a row to change it:

  • Position: the places the selected layout offers, plus Hidden. Corners shows poster-shaped tiles in a 3×3 grid, with a marker on the selected place, and Hidden is an icon button beside them; the other layouts list their places as pills. Each row's controls sit in a second column beside its label. Changing the layout re-labels every row. Dots is offered to quality only.
  • Show up to: how many tags the group shows, from 1 to 10. Quality and rating also offer All. Age rating and status always show one.
  • Include: the quality categories with their stack order, or the rating group's Community score and Critic score. Other groups have nothing to choose here.
  • Where to show: every group has the same six switches: Movies, Series, Seasons, Episodes, Continue Watching row and Next Up row. Turn one off to keep that group off those cards, for example genres off episodes or the age rating off the Next Up row. Each switch you have not changed follows the administrator's choice, and Follow server puts the whole group back on the administrator's choices. The item types also apply to Native Poster Tags. The two home rows are a web setting, because an app's image request does not say which row a poster is in. The live preview applies the switches to its sample movie, series and episode. People Tags appear on cast cards, not on media cards, so they have no switches. The item editor does not have them either, since they are set for all titles here. Collections and other videos always show the group. Rating works the same way: a Rating switch you turned off before this release stays off, and the others follow the administrator.
  • Show up to reads Always one tag for Status, Age rating and a one-logo Logos group, on the hub and in the item editor.

The limit applies after each group's own filtering (quality categories, language grouping and priority, each group's Where to show switches). Reset to defaults restores the administrator's layout, density, positions, order and limits; your group switches and include choices stay.

Show up to appears only for groups that can show multiple chips. Status (including Leaving soon and direct play) and Age rating always have a limit of one. Logos hides the control when the administrator permits only one logo, and shows it when the maximum is two. Saved higher limits cannot increase these single-chip groups. The hub and administrator Layout defaults / Groups panels follow the same rule.

Setting Default What it does Personal: Tag Layout / admin: Default Tag Layout Corners Chooses one of the layouts above Personal: Label density / admin: Label density under Default look Full Compact shortens quality labels (Dolby Vision → DV, HDR10+ → HDR+, ATMOS 7.1 → ATMOS, Dolby Digital 5.1 → DD 5.1, Dolby Digital+ 5.1 → DD+ 5.1) and hides the critic score when a community score is shown Tag Groups order Status, quality, rating, age rating, language, genre, awards, logos, custom Priority order of the groups Show up to Genre 3, language 3, awards 2, custom 3; quality, rating and two-logo groups all Hidden for single-chip Status and Age rating, and for Logos when Logos per title is 1; these groups always cap at 1 Position — Quality / Genre / Language / Rating / Age Rating / Status Tags Corners: Top Left / Top Right / Bottom Left / Bottom Right / Bottom Right / Top Right Any of the nine anchors in the Corners layout; the admin Position selects set these defaults Admin / personal: Hide tags on hover Off Fades web poster tags when you hover over a card, making its buttons easier to see; new and overwritten personal settings take the admin value Admin: Disable Tags on Search Page Off Suppresses the poster tags on Jellyfin web search results, including age-rating and review chips; useful for compatibility with Gelato

Compact quality vocabulary is shared by web and native rendering. The canonical Full label remains the colour identity; normalized layouts detect AC-3 and DTS-HD explicitly. Audio aliases follow the TRaSH-Guides Audio Formats vocabulary, adapted from release names to stream titles, codecs and profiles: Atmos and Plus forms win before plain DD, and DTS-HD before DTS. E-AC-3, EAC3, DDP, DD+ and Dolby Digital Plus share the DD+ identity; an E-AC-3 track whose profile or title says JOC (Dolby's object coding) is DD+ ATMOS.

Full label (optional channel suffix) Compact Dolby Digital / Dolby Digital+ DD / DD+ (keeps channels, for example DD+ 5.1) DTS-HD MA / DTS-HD HRA / DTS-HD DTS-HD (keeps channels) TRUEHD / ATMOS / TRUEHD ATMOS / DD+ ATMOS / DTS-X / DTS (including DTS-ES) Keeps the canonical codec name (both Atmos carriers shorten to ATMOS); drops channels FLAC / PCM Keep their name and channels (FLAC 2.0, PCM 7.1) AAC / Opus / MP3 Channel-only fallback (for example 5.1 or 7.1); stereo has no sound chip Dolby Vision / HDR10+ / BluRay DV / HDR+ / BD

Other emitted video codec labels (AV1, HEVC, H265, VP9, H264, VP8, XVID, DIVX, WMV, MPEG2, MPEG4, MJPEG, THEORA) are already short and remain unchanged.

AC-3 tracks produce Dolby Digital 5.1 in Full and DD 5.1 in Compact (E-AC-3 uses Dolby Digital+ 5.1 / DD+ 5.1). DTS-HD Master Audio and High Resolution remain distinct Full facts (DTS-HD MA / DTS-HD HRA) and both shorten to DTS-HD, retaining channels. A track that only says DTS-HD (no MA, XLL or Master Audio in its title or profile, and no HRA) is DTS-HD: JE does not claim it is lossless. Dolby TrueHD, Dolby Atmos and DTS:X stream aliases resolve to the established TRUEHD, ATMOS and DTS-X facts. The formatter also accepts their long names from portable or older cached labels; those aliases are not the detector’s canonical output. AAC, FLAC and Opus keep the existing channel-only fallback.

Existing version-0 Full layouts keep their previous audio labels until a layout setting is saved. This preserves their appearance; normalized layouts and Compact presentation use the codec facts above.

Compact labels on real library files: DD+ 5.1, DD 5.1, DTS-HD 5.1, BD, REMUX, IMAX, Ext and DC.

The four default corners keep their original appearance. Top and bottom centre wrap chips into centred rows (up to two); left and right centre stack chips vertically. Centre rows reserve the width occupied by corner groups, including a tall column from the opposite edge that reaches into the row on a short image, and each keeps to its half of the image; side columns reserve the height of their neighbouring corner stacks. Chips that are too wide or tall are hidden whole and counted in a +N chip, which names the hidden tags on hover or focus. Group limits apply before fitting.

Top-right groups move below Jellyfin's watched or unplayed-count indicator. Top centre reserves space for side indicators; in Flush it stays on the edge while the first chip fits that gap, and falls below indicators only when needed and only while it stays in the image's top half. On a short image crowded with tags (an episode still with every group on), a centre row with no room left even for a +N chip is left out; its tags stay in the card's hover description. Default and Tight keep their existing clearance. Bottom centre clears a card's progress bar; Flush meets the bar's top edge. People Tags have their own cast-card layout and no position.

At the left and right centre anchors, genre names appear toward the inside of the card on hover.

With Hide tags on hover off, genre names expand beside their icons on hover. Turn it on to fade poster tags instead.

Genre names expand with Hide Tags on Hover off; turning it on fades the tags instead.

docs.title: Admin defaults
docs.text:
The Layout defaults section of the Media Tags admin tab sets what new users start with: the layout, density, group order, each group's position per layout and the limits. In Corners a group's position is one of nine anchors on a small poster (these are the group's old Position settings) or Hidden; pick another default layout to set its positions. A group's row is greyed out while it is off for new users. The order and limits are only stored once you change them.

Upgrades, defaults, and limits
  • Settings saved before layouts existed keep the Corners layout, your corner choices, full labels, the original stacking order and limits.
